chair_narrative: R38 supports a large, precise adverse crude association of CRP >=10 mg/L with PFS among stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib (signed estimate 0.452 log-months, 95% CI 0.430–0.474), far exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold for 10% clinical importance. I accept only the specified within-sotorasib prognostic association. It does not support a causal CRP effect, sotorasib benefit, or CRP-specific treatment prediction: conditioning on treatment may induce selection bias, while disease burden, treatment line, functional status, steroid use, inflammatory comorbidity, molecular factors, and access remain uncontrolled competing explanations. Its close concordance with crude CRP contrasts across other treatment and clinical subgroups, plus the near-null CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (R18), argues against a treatment-specific interpretation. The peer drafts agree; I close investigation because further unadjusted validation would not resolve these limitations.

peer_narratives: I propose a bounded exploratory prognostic screen of the six previously unexamined research assays among stage-IV patients. For each standardized signature, the contrast is a one-unit increase; for markers, it is positive versus negative. Their biological roles are explicitly unspecified, so the anticipated raw direction is uncertain and the positive claim direction is only a reporting convention, not a prior assertion of benefit. Any detected effect should be judged against roughly 0.095 log-months for clinical importance and regarded as a crude association only. Plausible alternatives include chance from multiple testing, correlation with disease burden, inflammation, treatment allocation or line, performance status, molecular subtype, or assay construction rather than a biologically actionable prognostic mechanism.

Test whether the large adverse high-CRP prognostic association extends to stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib. Based on the consistent approximately 0.45 log-month adverse contrasts across stage, functional-status, albumin, NLR, brain-metastasis, and pembrolizumab-defined populations (including R10, R13, R15, R17, R21, R34, R35, R37), I expect shorter PFS for CRP >=10 mg/L, plausibly exceeding the 0.095 log-month clinical-significance threshold. This is a robustness/prognostic comparison, not a treatment-effect claim. Alternative explanations include treatment selection and line, tumor burden, inflammatory comorbidity, steroids, functional status, molecular features, and access; a result similar to prior contrasts would not establish a causal CRP effect or sotorasib-specific prediction.
chair_narrative: I prioritize a treatment-stratified refinement of the replicated adverse high-CRP prognostic association: among stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib, CRP >=10 mg/L is expected to be associated with shorter PFS than CRP <10 mg/L. The expected adverse association is supported by its consistency across stage, functional-status, albumin, NLR, metastatic-burden, and pembrolizumab-defined populations (R10, R13–R17, R20–R22, R34–R35, R37); an effect of at least 0.095 log-months would meet the prespecified clinical-importance threshold. This comparison estimates prognosis within a selected treatment group, not sotorasib benefit or CRP-based treatment prediction. Plausible alternatives are treatment selection and line, disease burden, performance status, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid use, molecular subtype, access, and chance; the near-null CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (R18) also cautions against expecting treatment-specific heterogeneity. I do not advance a broad screen of biologically unspecified constructed assays, since it would be a low-prior, multiple-testing exercise without a meaningful mechanistic hypothesis.

peer_narratives:
Supported findings: High CRP (>=10 mg/L) has a large, precise adverse crude association with PFS across stage-IV populations and within sotorasib-treated stage-IV patients (H33; R38). The signed 0.452 log-month estimate corresponds to an approximately 36% lower PFS on the raw scale and greatly exceeds the ~0.095 log-month threshold for 10% clinical importance. This pattern is concordant with independently validated high-CRP findings (H10, H13, H15, H17; R13, R16, R19, R22) and with stage-IV disease itself (H12; R12, R26).

Negative findings: Tested treatment-biomarker interactions and selected-treatment contrasts were near null or bounded well below clinical importance; this includes the CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (H16; R18). Thus, the evidence does not support clinically important treatment-effect modification by the tested markers. It also does not establish treatment equivalence or absence of smaller effects.

Unresolved uncertainty: These are crude observational comparisons. High CRP is supported as a prognostic correlate, not as a causal determinant of PFS, a sotorasib-specific finding, or a treatment-selection biomarker. Treatment allocation and line, disease burden, ECOG, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, molecular factors, and access remain plausible confounders. Counterintuitive crude ECOG and NLR results (R7, R11) further demonstrate that unadjusted contrasts are not reliable causal estimates.

Most informative next analysis: conduct a prespecified multivariable CRP prognostic analysis with adjustment for stage, metastatic burden, ECOG, albumin, NLR, laboratory measures, molecular variables, and treatment/line proxies, followed by independent-cohort assessment of calibration and stability. Further unadjusted subgroup searches would add little.

Supported findings: High CRP (>=10 mg/L) is consistently associated with substantially shorter PFS in crude comparisons, including among stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib (H33; R38, signed adverse contrast 0.452 log-months, 95% CI 0.430–0.474). This far exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold corresponding to 10% clinical importance. Similar magnitude across clinical and treatment-defined subsets supports a robust prognostic association rather than a sotorasib-specific observation.

Negative findings: Available treatment-biomarker interactions and treatment-specific interpretations are near-null or clinically small, including the CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (H16; R18). Thus, the evidence does not support CRP as a predictor of differential treatment benefit.

Unresolved uncertainty: These are crude observational contrasts. Conditioning on treatment and unmeasured treatment line, disease burden, ECOG, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, molecular factors, and access may substantially confound prognostic associations. The H33 result is not evidence that CRP causally worsens PFS or that sotorasib benefit differs by CRP.

Most informative next analysis: prespecify a multivariable CRP prognostic analysis jointly accounting for stage/metastatic burden, ECOG, albumin, NLR, laboratory variables, molecular features, and treatment/line proxies, followed by independent-cohort validation of calibration and effect stability.
chair_narrative:
Supported findings: High CRP (>=10 mg/L) has a large, precise adverse crude association with PFS in stage-IV disease and within stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib (H33; R38: signed adverse contrast 0.452 log-months, 95% CI 0.430–0.474). On the raw scale this corresponds to approximately 36% shorter PFS and greatly exceeds the 0.095 log-month threshold for 10% clinical importance. This is concordant with independently validated stage-IV CRP findings (H10, H13, H15, H17; R13, R16, R19, R22), with other clinical subgroups, and with the stage-IV association itself (H12; R12, R26).

Negative findings: Tested treatment–biomarker interactions and selected-treatment comparisons were near null or bounded below clinical importance, including the CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (H16; R18). Thus, these data do not support clinically important differential treatment benefit by the tested biomarkers. They do not establish treatment equivalence or exclude smaller effects.

Unresolved uncertainty: All results are crude observational contrasts. High CRP is supported as a prognostic correlate, including within a selected sotorasib-treated population, but not as a causal determinant of PFS, a sotorasib-specific finding, or a treatment-selection biomarker. Treatment allocation and line, disease burden, ECOG, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, molecular factors, and access remain plausible confounders; conditioning on treatment may also introduce selection bias. Counterintuitive crude ECOG and NLR results (R7, R11) reinforce this limitation. The peer drafts agree with this interpretation; I retain the within-sotorasib result as a clinically important crude prognostic association, not a predictive or causal conclusion.

Most informative next analysis: a prespecified adjusted CRP prognostic model incorporating stage/metastatic burden, ECOG, albumin, NLR, other laboratory measures, molecular variables, and treatment/line proxies, followed by independent-cohort evaluation of calibration and effect stability. Further unadjusted subgroup searches would add little.

peer_narratives: Run H34, the prespecified Welch interaction analysis among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients. Estimate whether the crude sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib log-PFS contrast is less favorable with CRP >=10 mg/L than with lower CRP. Evaluate the signed interaction and 95% interval against 0.095 log-months (approximately a 10% relative PFS difference), report all four cell sizes, and verify the minimum-cell diagnostic. This observational interaction remains susceptible to treatment-selection, treatment-line, disease-severity, and inflammatory-confounding biases; it would indicate differential crude association rather than causal treatment-effect heterogeneity.

Run H34, the prespecified crude Welch interaction among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients: whether the sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib log-PFS contrast is less favorable with CRP >=10 mg/L than with lower CRP. Report four cell sizes and the signed interaction estimate with 95% interval. A magnitude of about 0.095 log-months corresponds to the 10% clinical-significance threshold. This analysis addresses predictive heterogeneity rather than the already-established adverse prognostic CRP association; it remains vulnerable to confounding of treatment allocation, treatment line, disease burden, functional status, inflammatory comorbidity, molecular co-features, and selection.
chair_narrative: Run H34, the prespecified crude Welch interaction analysis among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients. Estimate whether the sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib log-PFS contrast is less favorable with CRP >=10 mg/L than with lower CRP. Report the signed interaction, 95% interval, all four cell sizes, and the minimum-cell diagnostic; assess clinical importance against 0.095 log-months (approximately a 10% relative PFS difference). This estimates crude predictive heterogeneity, not a causal treatment-effect interaction, and remains vulnerable to treatment allocation and line, disease burden, functional status, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, molecular co-features, and selection bias.

peer_narratives: H34 is not supported. The signed adverse interaction is only 0.012 log-months (95% CI -0.065 to 0.088), far below the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold for a 10% relative PFS difference; even the adverse-compatible bound does not reach that threshold. Although the cell-size rule is met, the CRP-high sotorasib cell is small (n=229), and this is a crude observational interaction vulnerable to differential treatment allocation, line of therapy, disease burden, performance status, inflammatory comorbidity, steroids, and molecular co-features. It also follows multiple subgroup comparisons. The data therefore provide no evidence for clinically important CRP-specific sotorasib benefit heterogeneity, and further unadjusted validation would not resolve the central confounding limitations.

R39 provides no evidence that high CRP produces a clinically important adverse sotorasib-by-CRP interaction among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients. The signed estimate is near null (0.012 log-months), and its 95% interval (-0.065 to 0.088) excludes the prespecified approximately 0.095 log-month threshold for a 10% relative PFS difference in the hypothesized adverse direction. Although the minimum cell is modest (n=229), it meets the analysis requirement and is sufficiently precise to reject this clinically meaningful crude interaction. This does not demonstrate equal treatment effects or causal absence of heterogeneity: treatment allocation, treatment line, disease severity, inflammatory comorbidity, ECOG, steroid use, and molecular co-features remain uncontrolled.
chair_narrative: H34 is rejected. The signed adverse CRP-by-sotorasib interaction is 0.012 log-months (95% CI −0.065 to 0.088), near null and with its adverse-compatible bound below the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold for a 10% relative PFS difference. All cells meet the minimum-size criterion, though the CRP-high sotorasib cell is modest (n=229). This rules out a clinically important crude adverse interaction at the specified threshold, not smaller heterogeneity or causal effect modification. Moreover, treatment allocation and line, disease burden, ECOG, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, and molecular co-features remain uncontrolled; further unadjusted validation would not address these limitations. The peer drafts agree with this conclusion.

peer_narratives: Test whether high CRP predicts differential sotorasib-associated PFS, rather than merely worse prognosis within sotorasib-treated patients. The interaction compares the sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib contrast in CRP >=10 mg/L patients against that contrast in CRP <10 mg/L patients; a negative result would indicate less favorable relative PFS with sotorasib in the high-CRP subgroup. I am uncertain a priori, because the large adverse CRP prognostic association within sotorasib-treated stage-IV patients (H33/R38) does not establish prediction, and the near-null CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction (H16/R18) reduces expectation of treatment-specific heterogeneity. An interaction magnitude of about 0.095 log-months or greater would be clinically important. Plausible alternatives to any observed interaction include nonrandom treatment allocation, treatment line, molecular eligibility, disease burden, performance status, inflammatory comorbidity, and conditioning/selection effects.

I propose a prespecified predictive refinement: among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients, test whether the crude sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib PFS contrast is less favorable in those with CRP >=10 mg/L than in those with lower CRP. High CRP is a large adverse prognostic correlate across populations, including sotorasib-treated patients (R38), so attenuation of apparent treatment benefit is plausible and clinically relevant if at least 0.095 log-months. This interaction, unlike H33, directly addresses heterogeneity of the treatment contrast. However, it remains observational: treatment line, disease severity, eligibility, co-medications, molecular co-features, and selection into sotorasib can generate an apparent interaction. H24's near-null overall KRAS-G12C treatment contrast also makes a large differential benefit uncertain.
chair_narrative: Test whether, among stage-IV KRAS-G12C patients, the crude sotorasib-versus-no-sotorasib PFS contrast is less favorable in patients with CRP >=10 mg/L than in those with lower CRP. A negative interaction of at least 0.095 log-months would meet the 10% clinical-importance threshold. High CRP has a large adverse prognostic association within sotorasib-treated patients (H33/R38), but that finding does not establish predictive utility; H24/R29 also found a near-null overall crude sotorasib contrast. I therefore register an uncertain rather than adverse anticipated interaction. I adopt the KRAS-G12C restriction proposed by peer 2 because it is clinically and biologically coherent for sotorasib; peer 1's broader stage-IV population would include many patients outside the molecularly relevant treatment population. Plausible alternatives to an observed interaction include confounding by treatment line, treatment allocation, disease burden, ECOG, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid use, molecular co-features, and selection induced by conditioning on treatment eligibility.

peer_narratives:
Supported finding: elevated CRP (>=10 mg/L) is a large, precise crude adverse prognostic correlate of PFS. In stage-IV disease it is independently replicated (H10; R10, R13), persists in clinically selected strata (H13, H15, H17), is similar in non-stage-IV disease (H18), and is present among sotorasib-treated stage-IV patients (H33; R38). Effects near -0.45 log-months correspond to roughly 36% shorter PFS, well beyond the 10% clinical-significance threshold. This supports prognostic association, not causality or treatment-selection utility.

Negative findings: no tested treatment–biomarker interaction supports clinically important differential benefit. In particular, the new CRP-by-sotorasib interaction in stage-IV KRAS-G12C disease is near null (H34; R39, signed adverse estimate 0.012, 95% CI -0.065 to 0.088 log-months); even its adverse-compatible bound is below the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold. Other tested treatment interactions and molecularly selected crude treatment contrasts were likewise null or bounded below clinical importance.

Uncertainty: all comparisons are unadjusted observational contrasts. CRP may reflect disease burden, systemic inflammation, treatment line/allocation, performance status, comorbidity, steroid exposure, laboratory status, molecular features, or access rather than a causal driver. The within-treatment CRP association cannot establish predictive effect modification and conditioning on treatment may introduce selection bias. Counterintuitive crude ECOG and NLR associations further demonstrate that these data should not be used for causal treatment inference.

Most informative next analysis: prespecify an adjusted CRP prognostic analysis using available baseline stage, ECOG, metastatic burden proxy, albumin, NLR, other laboratory variables, molecular variables, and treatment indicators, then test effect stability in an independent cohort. Further unadjusted subgroup searches are unlikely to materially improve the conclusion.

Supported: CRP >=10 mg/L is a large, precise adverse crude prognostic correlate of PFS in stage-IV disease (H10; R10, R13), persisting in several clinically selected subsets including ECOG <2, preserved albumin, low NLR, no brain metastases, and sotorasib-treated patients (H13–H15, H17, H29–H33). Effects are approximately 0.45 log-months, far exceeding the 0.095 log-month clinical-significance threshold, and key results have independent validation.

Negative: The tested treatment-biomarker interactions, including CRP-by-sotorasib in KRAS-G12C disease (H34; R39), are near null or have intervals excluding a clinically important adverse interaction at the prespecified threshold. The data therefore do not support using the tested biomarkers as crude treatment-selection predictors. They do not establish treatment equivalence or exclude smaller heterogeneity.

Unresolved: These are unadjusted observational contrasts. CRP should be interpreted as a robust prognostic association rather than a causal determinant or treatment-specific predictive biomarker. Confounding by disease burden, performance status, treatment allocation/line, inflammation-related comorbidity, steroids, molecular features, and selection from treatment conditioning remains material; counterintuitive crude ECOG and NLR associations underscore this concern.

chair_narrative:
Supported finding: CRP >=10 mg/L is a large, precise adverse crude prognostic correlate of PFS. In stage-IV disease it is independently replicated (H10; R10, R13), persists in clinically selected strata (H13, H15, H17), is similar outside stage IV (H18), and is also present among sotorasib-treated stage-IV patients (H33; R38). Effects near 0.45 log-months imply roughly 36% shorter PFS and clearly exceed the approximately 0.095 log-month threshold for 10% clinical importance.

Negative finding: No tested treatment–biomarker interaction supports clinically important crude differential benefit. Most recently, the CRP-by-sotorasib interaction in stage-IV KRAS-G12C disease is near null (H34; R39: signed adverse estimate 0.012, 95% CI -0.065 to 0.088 log-months); even its adverse-compatible bound is below the clinical-importance threshold. Other tested interactions and molecularly selected crude treatment contrasts were likewise null or bounded below clinical importance. This does not establish treatment equivalence or rule out smaller heterogeneity.

Unresolved uncertainty: These are unadjusted observational contrasts. CRP is supported as a robust prognostic association, not as a causal determinant, sotorasib-specific factor, or treatment-selection biomarker. Disease burden, performance status, treatment allocation and line, inflammatory comorbidity, steroid exposure, molecular co-features, and access may confound results; conditioning on treatment can introduce selection bias. The counterintuitive crude ECOG and NLR results (R7, R11) further caution against causal interpretation. The peer drafts agree on these conclusions; I retain the within-sotorasib CRP result only as a prognostic association.

Most informative next analysis: prespecify an adjusted CRP prognostic model including stage/metastatic-burden proxies, ECOG, albumin, NLR, other laboratory measures, molecular factors, and treatment/line proxies, then test calibration and effect stability in an independent cohort. Further unadjusted subgroup searches are unlikely to materially improve the inference.

Unresolved uncertainty: the repeated crude CRP findings may reflect disease burden, performance status, inflammatory/infectious comorbidity, treatment line and allocation, molecular factors, and selection induced by conditioning on treatment. Thus their biological and causal interpretation remains uncertain.

Most informative next analysis: prespecify an adjusted treatment-by-CRP interaction analysis in an appropriate treatment-eligible population, incorporating treatment line/allocation, baseline disease burden, ECOG status, laboratory and inflammatory covariates, and molecular predictors, then independently evaluate it. Further unadjusted treatment-stratum comparisons would add little.

H56/R67 supports a clinically meaningful descriptive marker-D association in non-stage-IV disease (+0.143 log-months, 95% CI +0.129 to +0.157), with the entire interval exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-month clinical-significance benchmark. Together with the previously near-null stage interaction, this supports consistency of the descriptive association across stage strata, not a causal, prognostic, or biological interpretation: marker D is constructed and unassigned, and confounding, selection, care patterns, or a D-specific outcome-generation artifact remain plausible.

H57/R68 provides precise negative evidence for clinically meaningful modification of the stage-IV marker-D association by having none versus any of the four recorded treatments (interaction +0.001, 95% CI -0.026 to +0.029). The interval excludes a clinically important approximately 0.095 log-month interaction, so the interaction claim is rejected. This null interaction does not eliminate treatment-related selection, unrecorded treatments, or other confounding of the underlying marker-D contrasts.
chair_narrative:
H56/R67 supports a clinically meaningful descriptive association in non-stage-IV disease: marker-D positivity is associated with +0.143 log-months PFS (95% CI +0.129 to +0.157), entirely above the approximately 0.095 log-month 10% clinical-significance threshold. Together with the previously near-null stage interaction, this supports descriptive consistency across stage strata. It does not establish a causal, independent prognostic, or biological effect: D is constructed, and residual disease-severity, care-pathway, selection, measurement, and D-specific outcome-generation artifacts remain plausible amid extensive exploration.

H57/R68 is precise negative evidence for clinically meaningful modification of the stage-IV marker-D association by none versus any of the four recorded treatments (interaction +0.001 log-months, 95% CI -0.026 to +0.029). The interval excludes an interaction of approximately 0.095 log-months, so the positive interaction claim is rejected. This null result does not control treatment confounding or exclude unrecorded treatment and selection/collider bias induced by conditioning on recorded treatment status.

peer_narratives: Prioritize the already registered H56 direct contrast: marker-D positivity versus negativity among non-stage-IV patients. The anticipated direction is positive but uncertainty remains because D is a constructed assay. This estimates generalizability directly; a signed effect of at least approximately 0.095 log-months would meet the clinical-significance benchmark. Together with H51/R62 and the near-null stage interaction H55/R66, it can distinguish a broadly similar descriptive association from an imprecise inference based solely on interaction testing.

Marker-D positivity is associated with longer PFS overall in stage-IV disease (H51/R62) and in patients receiving none of the four recorded treatments (H54/R65), both clinically meaningful descriptively. This interaction directly tests whether the association is materially stronger in the no-recorded-treatment subgroup than in its complement, rather than inferring heterogeneity from separate estimates. The expected direction is uncertain: a positive interaction could indicate treatment-allocation, selection, or care-pathway structure, whereas a near-null interaction would suggest that recorded-treatment status does not materially modify the descriptive association. As D is a constructed marker, either result remains noncausal and nonbiological.
chair_narrative: H56 remains the priority direct estimate of marker-D association in non-stage-IV disease; it quantifies generalizability rather than relying only on H55’s near-null stage interaction. I additionally register a direct stage-IV interaction by recorded-treatment status. H51/R62 and H54/R65 show similar clinically meaningful descriptive associations (+0.151 and +0.153 log-months), but only an interaction can test whether their apparent similarity reflects genuinely little treatment-status heterogeneity. The anticipated direction is uncertain; an interaction of at least about 0.095 log-months would suggest materially stronger association among patients without recorded treatment, while a near-null result would argue against recorded-treatment status as an important modifier. Neither result supports causal or biological interpretation of constructed marker D.

peer_narratives:
Supported descriptive findings: poor performance status (H43/R7,R54) and high NLR (H44/R11) each correspond to approximately +0.45 log-months in the specified unfavorable direction in stage-IV disease (about a 57% PFS contrast), with narrow intervals well beyond the 10% clinical-significance threshold. High CRP shows a similarly large, replicated unfavorable association across stage, prognosis, and recorded-treatment restrictions (e.g., H10/R10,R13; H13/R14,R16; H40/R50,R51), including EGFR-mutant/osimertinib-treated strata (H35/R40,R41; H36/R43,R44). These are highly precise observational associations, not causal effects.

Marker-D positivity is associated descriptively with longer PFS in both stage-IV (H51/R62, +0.151 log-months) and non-stage-IV disease (H56/R67, +0.143); both exceed the approximately 0.095 log-month clinical threshold. The stage interaction is near null (H55/R66), and recorded-treatment-status interaction is also precisely near null (H57/R68), supporting descriptive consistency rather than meaningful effect modification.

Negative findings: the tested targeted-treatment and pembrolizumab contrasts/interactions do not demonstrate clinically meaningful benefit or biomarker modification (H1–H6, H16, H23–H25, H34, H37, H39, H42). Most tested heterogeneity claims for CRP, stage, histology, ECOG, NLR, and marker D are similarly null or clinically trivial. Markers E and F have near-null associations (H52/R63; H53/R64).

Uncertainty remains substantial for causal, independent prognostic, and biological interpretation. All estimates are unadjusted Welch contrasts; confounding by disease severity, treatment selection, unrecorded care, measurement/coding, and outcome-generation artifacts can explain associations. Constructed marker D has no assigned biological role, so its replicated descriptive association should not be treated as a biomarker mechanism or clinical decision rule. The most informative next analysis, if further work were available, would be a prespecified multivariable/causal analysis of marker D and the major prognostic variables with treatment and baseline-severity adjustment, followed by independent validation; this final iteration has no remaining validation requests.

Final synthesis: high CRP (>=10 mg/L) and stage-IV status are consistently associated with substantially shorter observed PFS (H10/R10,R13; H12/R12,R26), with signed effects about 0.45 log-months in the adverse direction—far exceeding the ~0.095 log-month clinical-significance threshold. The high-CRP association persists across examined clinical and recorded-treatment restrictions, including H13–H18, H29–H40. These are robust descriptive findings, not causal effects.

ECOG >=2 and NLR >=3 show large associations in the opposite, counterintuitive direction—longer observed PFS (H43/R7,R54; H44/R11; H45–H50)—also about 0.45 log-months. Their consistency across selected strata makes them empirical dataset findings, but their clinical interpretation is unresolved because the direction is biologically unexpected and may reflect selection, coding, care-pathway, or outcome-generation structure.

Research-marker-D positivity is descriptively associated with longer PFS in stage-IV disease (H51/R62, +0.151 log-months) and non-stage-IV disease (H56/R67, +0.143); both exceed clinical significance. Near-null stage and recorded-treatment-status interactions (H55/R66; H57/R68) argue against clinically meaningful heterogeneity by those factors. Markers E and F are negative controls with near-null associations (H52/R63; H53/R64). D remains non-biological and non-causal: constructed-assay artifacts and unmeasured confounding remain unresolved.

Negative findings include no clinically meaningful evidence for the prespecified treatment biomarker interactions or within-biomarker treatment contrasts (H1–H6, H16, H23–H25, H34, H37, H39, H42), and no meaningful CRP effect modification by stage, NLR, ECOG, albumin, histology, or the assessed therapies. The most informative next analysis would be an independently held-out, covariate-adjusted prognostic analysis of marker D and the anomalous ECOG/NLR associations, with explicit treatment timing and care-pathway variables; this is needed before interpreting any association as clinically or biologically meaningful.
chair_narrative:
Supported descriptive findings: high CRP (>=10 mg/L) and stage-IV status are each associated with substantially shorter observed PFS (H10/R10,R13; H12/R12,R26), with adverse-direction contrasts of about 0.45 log-months, far exceeding the ~0.095 log-month (10%) clinical-significance threshold. The CRP association is consistent across examined clinical and recorded-treatment restrictions, including EGFR-mutant/osimertinib-treated and no-recorded-treatment subsets (H13–H18, H29–H40). These are precise observational associations, not causal effects.

ECOG >=2 and NLR >=3 are associated with longer observed PFS in this dataset (H43/R7,R54; H44/R11), also about +0.45 log-months. Their magnitude and consistency across selected strata support them as empirical descriptive findings, but the direction is clinically counterintuitive; selection, coding, care-pathway, confounding, or outcome-generation structure may explain it.

Research-marker-D positivity is descriptively associated with longer PFS in stage-IV disease (H51/R62, +0.151 log-months) and non-stage-IV disease (H56/R67, +0.143), both clinically meaningful. Near-null stage and recorded-treatment-status interactions (H55/R66; H57/R68) provide negative evidence for clinically meaningful heterogeneity. Markers E and F have near-null associations (H52/R63; H53/R64).

Negative findings include no clinically meaningful evidence for the tested targeted-treatment or pembrolizumab contrasts/interactions, or most tested CRP effect-modification claims (H1–H6, H16, H19–H28, H34, H39, H41–H42). H37 remains imprecise rather than affirmative evidence of osimertinib-by-CRP modification.

The drafts agree on the main results; I retain the explicit caution that ECOG/NLR findings are descriptive and anomalous, rather than labeling them prognostic benefits. Causal, independent prognostic, and biological interpretations remain unresolved for all unadjusted Welch contrasts, especially constructed marker D. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified covariate-adjusted and temporally well-defined prognostic/causal analysis of marker D and the anomalous ECOG/NLR associations, incorporating baseline severity, treatment timing, and care-pathway variables, followed by external validation.

peer_narratives: Request Welch 95% discovery estimates for all preregistered treatment–biomarker interactions and baseline prognostic contrasts. I will judge clinical importance against 0.095 log-months (approximately a 10% PFS ratio) in the stated direction, requiring estimates and intervals to support both direction and magnitude. Treatment contrasts are observational and unadjusted, so apparent interactions may reflect indication, line, co-treatment, biomarker correlation, or baseline prognosis; interaction estimates are nevertheless the appropriate initial test of biomarker-specific effects. Diagnostics should include comparison-cell sizes (minimum 20 required) and interval precision; null or subclinical results will be recorded as such rather than interpreted as evidence of benefit.

Request all preregistered comparisons. Analyses should use the specified unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator Welch estimates, with interaction contrasts evaluated within stage-IV eligibility. I will interpret effects on the log-PFS scale against the clinical-importance threshold of 0.095 log units (about a 10% relative PFS difference), considering interval precision, subgroup cell sizes, and the non-causal nature of treatment and prognostic associations.
chair_narrative: Request discovery estimates for all preregistered treatment–biomarker interactions and baseline prognostic contrasts. Use the specified unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator Welch estimates; interactions remain restricted to stage-IV eligibility. Interpret signed effects against 0.095 log-PFS (approximately a 10% PFS ratio), considering 95% interval precision and the requirement for at least 20 observations per comparison cell. Treatment associations are observational and may be confounded by indication, treatment line, co-treatment, correlated biomarkers, and baseline prognosis; prognostic contrasts are likewise unadjusted.

peer_narratives: R1–R6 show no clinically meaningful biomarker-by-treatment interaction: all signed estimates are far below the prespecified 0.095 log-PFS threshold, and even their upper bounds do not approach that threshold. R3 is less precise but still excludes a clinically important benefit. R5 and R6 are directionally contrary. These are unadjusted observational interactions, so even a small nominal signal would be vulnerable to confounding by indication, line of therapy, co-treatment, molecular correlation, and prognostic biomarker effects; none warrants follow-up. R7 and R10 show large, highly precise adverse prognostic associations in their prespecified directions, comfortably exceeding clinical significance despite multiplicity. They support associations, not causal effects, since baseline disease severity and correlated prognostic factors remain plausible explanations. R8 and R11 are precise nulls, while R9 and R12 are large but opposite to their registered adverse-direction claims and therefore reject those claims. I request replication of H7 because its magnitude is substantial and stage is a broad clinical prognostic factor susceptible to case-mix confounding, although the claim as stated is an association.

All six stage-IV biomarker-treatment interactions are far below the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance threshold, and their 95% intervals exclude that threshold in the proposed direction (R1-R6). They do not support clinically meaningful predictive benefit or attenuation; the unadjusted design would additionally remain vulnerable to indication, line-of-therapy, co-treatment, and correlated-biomarker confounding. Stage IV and CRP >=10 are each associated with substantially shorter PFS in the proposed direction (R7, R10; roughly 36% lower PFS on the raw ratio scale), so these descriptive prognostic contrasts meet the clinical threshold, though they are not causal effects. Brain metastases and low albumin show near-null raw contrasts (R8, R11). ECOG >=2 and NLR >=3 are strongly contrary to their proposed adverse-prognosis directions (R9, R12), an implausible pattern that raises concern for selection, treatment allocation, coding, or other severe confounding rather than a credible protective interpretation. I reject those original directional claims and prioritize an independent check of the more clinically anomalous ECOG result.
chair_narrative: R1-R6 provide no evidence for clinically meaningful biomarker-by-treatment interactions: every signed estimate and 95% upper bound is below the prespecified 0.095 log-PFS threshold. The observational, unadjusted interactions would in any event be susceptible to treatment indication, treatment line, co-treatment, baseline prognosis, and biomarker correlation. R7 and R10 show large, precise adverse raw PFS associations in their prespecified directions, comfortably exceeding the clinical threshold; I accept these only as unadjusted descriptive/prognostic associations, not causal or independently adjusted effects. R8 and R11 are precise nulls. R9 and R12 are large and precise in the direction opposite their registered adverse claims, so the original claims are rejected. Their apparent favorable associations for poor ECOG and high NLR are clinically anomalous and more plausibly reflect coding, selection, treatment allocation, or severe confounding than protective biology. This resolves the draft disagreement by accepting H7 without requiring replication, while prioritizing scrutiny of the anomalous H9 result.

peer_narratives: I prioritize prespecified treatment-by-biomarker interactions in stage IV disease, where the clinical question is whether the treatment contrast is enriched in a molecularly defined population rather than whether the biomarker is merely prognostic. Expected positive enrichment is strongest for EGFR/osimertinib and KRAS G12C/sotorasib, with plausible enrichment for high PD-L1 or high TMB with pembrolizumab and BRCA2 alteration with olaparib. STK11 mutation is hypothesized to attenuate pembrolizumab benefit. On the log outcome scale, effects near or above 0.095 correspond approximately to the stated 10% clinical-significance threshold. These are observational crude contrasts: confounding by treatment indication, line of therapy, unmeasured co-treatments, biomarker correlation, and differential baseline prognosis are credible alternatives to genuine predictive effects; null or subclinical estimates would not support clinically meaningful biomarker-guided benefit.

I prioritize prespecified, biologically anchored treatment-effect heterogeneity: osimertinib in EGFR-mutant disease, sotorasib in KRAS-G12C disease, olaparib in BRCA2-mutant disease, and pembrolizumab in PD-L1-high or TMB-high disease. STK11 mutation is proposed as a falsifiable negative modifier of pembrolizumab benefit. I also propose established baseline adverse-prognostic factors in the full study population. These are unadjusted discovery contrasts and treatment comparisons may reflect allocation and prognosis rather than causal effects. A clinically important PFS contrast corresponds approximately to an absolute log-PFS difference of 0.095 or more (a 10% PFS ratio); conclusions should consider both this magnitude and interval precision. The next stage should analyze these registered comparisons, with particular attention to treatment-by-biomarker interaction estimates rather than main treatment effects.
chair_narrative: I register biomarker-by-treatment interactions in stage IV disease, where these systemic-treatment comparisons are clinically coherent. I resolve the draft disagreement over unrestricted versus stage-IV analyses in favor of the stage-IV restriction: early-stage patients may have different treatment intent and prognosis, making a pooled interaction less interpretable. Expected enrichment is positive for EGFR/osimertinib, KRAS-G12C/sotorasib, BRCA2/olaparib, and PD-L1-high or TMB-high disease/pembrolizumab; STK11 mutation is expected to attenuate pembrolizumab benefit. I also register adverse baseline prognostic contrasts. A clinically important result should be at least 0.095 log-PFS (approximately a 10% PFS ratio) in the stated direction. Raw treatment contrasts and interactions may instead reflect treatment indication, line of therapy, co-treatments, molecular correlation, or unequal baseline prognosis; biomarker prognostic effects could also be mistaken for prediction. Null, imprecise, or subclinical effects will not establish clinically meaningful biomarker-guided benefit.

peer_narratives: Independent validation R13 decisively rejects the original H9 claim: the signed estimate is -0.450 log-months (interval -0.467 to -0.432), meaning that, contrary to the registered adverse-direction hypothesis, ECOG PS >=2 has an approximately 0.45 higher unadjusted log-PFS association. This is far larger than the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance threshold and is consistent with R9, so it is not plausibly a chance finding. It supports only a reproducible unadjusted descriptive reversal, not a protective effect of poor performance status; treatment allocation, selection, disease-stage composition, or coding remain substantial unresolved explanations. The most informative next analysis is the same ECOG contrast restricted to stage-IV disease, to test whether mixing treatment intents/stages accounts for the anomalous overall association. H9 remains active only for this explanatory refinement, while its original adverse prognostic claim is rejected.

H9 is rejected and closed. The independent validation (R13) closely reproduces the discovery result (R9), with a large, precise estimate in the direction opposite the registered adverse-ECOG hypothesis. Its magnitude greatly exceeds the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance benchmark, so this is not compatible with merely a small adverse association. However, neither result supports a protective biological or causal interpretation of poor performance status: both are unadjusted observational contrasts, and the clinically anomalous reversal strongly suggests selection, coding, treatment-allocation, or other confounding. The most informative next analysis is the registered stage-IV-restricted refinement, which tests whether the reversed descriptive association remains after restricting to a more clinically homogeneous disease setting; it still would not establish an independent or causal prognostic effect.
chair_narrative: H9 is rejected: validation R13 closely reproduces R9, with a large, precise result opposite the registered adverse-direction claim. In raw terms, ECOG PS >=2 is associated with approximately 0.45 higher unadjusted log-PFS, and the validation interval remains far beyond the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance threshold. This supports a reproducible descriptive reversal, not a protective, independent, or causal effect of poor performance status. The clinically anomalous direction leaves coding, selection, treatment allocation, stage/treatment-intent mixture, and other confounding unresolved. I retain investigation as active because the most informative next analysis is the preregistered stage-IV-restricted ECOG contrast, testing whether the reversal persists in a more clinically homogeneous setting. This resolves the draft disagreement in favor of continued explanatory investigation rather than closing the inquiry, while maintaining rejection of the original claim.

peer_narratives: Request the four preregistered stage-focused analyses. They use unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator Welch contrasts (and the specified difference-in-differences interaction), so results will be descriptive rather than causal. The clinically meaningful threshold is approximately 0.095 log-PFS (log[1.10]). H13 and H14 test whether the anomalous favorable pooled associations of poor ECOG and high NLR persist within stage IV; H15 tests stage heterogeneity of the ECOG association; H16 tests whether the adverse raw CRP association persists in stage IV. Interpret intervals against both zero and the clinical threshold, while scrutinizing direction reversals as likely susceptible to selection, coding, treatment allocation, and residual confounding.

Request discovery analyses for all four preregistered stage-focused contrasts. They use unadjusted Welch exposed-minus-comparator estimates (and the specified difference-in-differences interaction), with 95% intervals and adequate cell-size diagnostics. I will judge clinical materiality against 0.095 log-PFS (approximately a 10% relative difference): an interval confined below that magnitude would argue against a clinically meaningful association, whereas an interval excluding zero and spanning or exceeding it would warrant investigation. These analyses can test whether the anomalous pooled ECOG and NLR reversals persist in stage-IV disease and whether ECOG’s association differs by stage, but cannot resolve coding, selection, treatment-allocation, or other confounding.
chair_narrative: Request the four preregistered stage-focused analyses using unadjusted Welch exposed-minus-comparator contrasts (and the specified difference-in-differences interaction). H13 and H14 test whether the anomalous favorable pooled associations of poor ECOG and high NLR persist within stage-IV disease; H15 tests whether the ECOG association differs by stage; H16 tests persistence of the adverse CRP association within stage IV. Interpret 95% intervals against zero and the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-materiality threshold. These descriptive analyses cannot distinguish coding, selection, treatment allocation, stage mixture, or residual confounding from biological or prognostic associations.

peer_narratives: Within stage-IV disease, R14 and R15 show large, precise favorable raw associations of poor ECOG and high NLR with log-PFS (about 0.45 log-months), far exceeding the 0.095 clinical-materiality threshold. I accept H13 and H14 only as reproducible unadjusted descriptive reversals, while keeping investigation active: their clinically implausible direction strongly raises coding, selection, treatment allocation, survivor/line-of-therapy, and residual-confounding explanations. R16 provides no evidence of a clinically meaningful ECOG-by-stage interaction; its interval is small and includes zero, so H15 is rejected. R17 shows a large, precise adverse raw CRP association within stage IV, supporting H16 descriptively but not causally or as an independent prognostic effect.

R14 and R15 show large, precise positive raw associations for ECOG PS >=2 and NLR >=3 within stage-IV disease (about 0.45 log-PFS each), far exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% relative difference. I accept H13 and H14 only as unadjusted descriptive associations and retain investigation because their clinically implausible favorable direction needs explanation. The persistence within stage IV weakens simple stage-mixture as the sole explanation, but does not address selection, coding, treatment indication/line, co-treatment, or residual prognostic confounding. R16 is a precise near-null ECOG-by-stage interaction, with its interval far below clinical materiality; reject H15. R17 confirms a large adverse raw CRP association within stage IV, supporting H16 descriptively; no causal or independent prognostic inference is warranted. Independent validation of H13 is requested because it is the most clinically anomalous newly restricted result.
chair_narrative: R14 and R15 show large, precise favorable raw associations of poor ECOG and high NLR with log-PFS within stage-IV disease (about 0.45 log-months), greatly exceeding the 0.095 clinical-materiality threshold. I accept H13 and H14 only as reproducible unadjusted descriptive reversals and keep investigation active. Persistence after stage restriction means stage mixture alone cannot explain them, but coding, selection, treatment indication or line, co-treatment, and residual prognostic confounding remain much more plausible than protective effects. R16 is a precise near-null ECOG-by-stage interaction, with its interval entirely below clinical materiality; H15 is rejected. R17 supports H16 as a large adverse raw CRP association within stage IV, but does not establish causality or an independent prognostic association. I request validation of H13 because its clinically anomalous restricted result is the highest-priority finding to reproduce.

peer_narratives: The priority is to determine whether the anomalous favorable raw associations for poor ECOG and high NLR reflect stage mixture rather than a clinically credible protective effect. H13 already evaluates ECOG within stage IV; I add the analogous stage-IV NLR contrast and an ECOG-by-stage interaction. A positive interaction would indicate that the unexpected ECOG association differs in stage-IV versus earlier-stage disease, supporting population-mixing or treatment-intent explanations rather than biology. I also refine the accepted adverse CRP association within stage IV to assess whether this descriptive prognostic signal is robust in the clinically relevant advanced-disease population. For all contrasts, effects of at least 0.095 log-PFS in the hypothesized direction would be clinically material; these remain unadjusted associations and cannot establish causal or independent prognostic effects.

The reproducible favorable raw association for poor ECOG status is clinically implausible as a protective effect and needs explanation in a more homogeneous stage-IV population. H13 directly tests that restriction for ECOG. I additionally propose the analogous stage-IV NLR contrast to determine whether the second anomalous reversal persists; a positive result of at least 0.095 log-PFS would indicate a clinically important descriptive reversal, not favorable biology. The ECOG-by-pembrolizumab interaction tests whether treatment allocation contributes to the anomaly: an uncertain interaction would be compatible with broad selection/confounding, whereas a sizable positive interaction would localize the reversal to one treatment stratum. All proposed comparisons remain unadjusted and cannot establish causal, independent prognostic, or treatment-benefit effects.
chair_narrative: I prioritize explanation of the clinically implausible favorable raw associations for poor ECOG and high NLR. The stage-IV NLR contrast tests whether the H12 reversal persists in a more prognostically homogeneous advanced-disease population; because stage mixture may explain the pooled result, its restricted-direction expectation is uncertain rather than assumed favorable. The ECOG-by-stage interaction directly tests whether the anomalous ECOG contrast differs between stage-IV and non-stage-IV disease. A positive interaction of at least 0.095 log-PFS would support stage-dependent selection, treatment-intent, or population-mixing explanations, not protective biology. I also test whether the accepted adverse raw CRP association remains clinically material within stage IV. This resolves the draft disagreement by favoring a stage interaction over a treatment-stratified ECOG analysis: treatment allocation is itself strongly confounded and would be less direct for testing the leading stage-mixture explanation. All comparisons are unadjusted descriptive associations; coding, selection, treatment allocation, and other confounding remain plausible alternatives.

peer_narratives: H13 is accepted as a reproducible, clinically material unadjusted descriptive association: among stage-IV patients, ECOG PS >=2 had approximately 0.46 higher log-PFS than ECOG <2 in validation (R18), closely corroborating discovery (R14). This magnitude substantially exceeds the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-materiality threshold. It does not support a causal or protective interpretation of poor performance status, nor establish an independent prognostic effect. The direction remains clinically anomalous and is compatible with selection, treatment allocation or line-of-therapy differences, coding/measurement issues, and residual confounding. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H14, to determine whether the similarly large favorable stage-IV association for high NLR is reproducible; joint reproducibility would prioritize investigation of shared selection or data-generation mechanisms over biological interpretation.

R18 independently reproduces H13: among stage-IV patients, ECOG PS >=2 has an approximately 0.46 log-month higher unadjusted PFS, with a narrow validation interval wholly beyond the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-materiality threshold. I therefore accept H13 as a robust descriptive association and keep it active. This does not support a protective biological, causal, or independent prognostic effect of poor performance status; the direction is clinically anomalous and remains compatible with selection, treatment allocation, coding, treatment intent, and residual confounding. The prior stage interaction was near null, so stage mixture alone is not an adequate explanation. The most informative next analysis is whether this reversal differs by pembrolizumab exposure within stage IV, which can test treatment-allocation heterogeneity while remaining explicitly descriptive.
chair_narrative: H13 is supported as a reproducible, clinically material unadjusted descriptive association: within stage-IV disease, ECOG PS >=2 was associated with about 0.46 higher log-PFS in both discovery and independent validation (R14, R18), far exceeding the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance threshold. This is not evidence that poor performance status is protective, causal, or independently prognostic. The precise but clinically anomalous direction, together with the near-null stage interaction (R16), argues that stage mixture alone is not an adequate explanation; selection, coding, treatment allocation/line, treatment intent, and residual confounding remain unresolved. I favor validating the parallel stage-IV high-NLR reversal (H14) next over immediately subdividing H13 by pembrolizumab: replication of that independent anomalous marker association is the more informative test of whether a shared data-generation or selection mechanism is plausible. The treatment-specific interaction remains a useful subsequent descriptive refinement if the anomaly persists.

peer_narratives: Run the three preregistered unadjusted stage-IV interaction analyses. Each estimates whether the exposed-minus-comparator association differs across the specified poor-risk subgroup versus its complement. I will judge intervals against both zero and approximately 0.095 log-PFS (the log-scale equivalent of a 10% relative difference). These analyses are exploratory/descriptive: even a clinically material interaction would not identify causal treatment-effect modification because treatment allocation, line/intent, coding, selection, and residual confounding are uncontrolled.

Run the three preregistered, unadjusted stage-IV interaction analyses. They use Welch independent-cell difference-in-differences, requiring at least 20 observations per cell, and test whether the anomalous favorable raw associations for poor ECOG or high NLR are attributable to pembrolizumab allocation or are concentrated in their joint subgroup. Interpret signed estimates and 95% intervals against zero and a clinically material threshold of 0.095 log-PFS. Existing evidence supports large descriptive reversals for H13/H14 but does not support a causal or protective interpretation; these interactions are mechanistic diagnostics rather than confirmation of benefit. No new effect estimates or null findings are available at this analyze action.
chair_narrative: Run the three preregistered unadjusted stage-IV interaction analyses (H17–H19). Each is a Welch independent-cell difference-in-differences analysis, requiring at least 20 observations per cell, testing whether the exposed-minus-comparator association differs in the specified poor-risk subgroup versus its complement. Interpret signed estimates and 95% intervals relative to zero and the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-materiality threshold. These are descriptive mechanism diagnostics only: treatment allocation, line/intent, coding, selection, and residual confounding preclude causal interpretation of any apparent effect modification.

peer_narratives: All three prespecified stage-IV interactions are near null, with 95% intervals far below the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-significance threshold. R19 provides no evidence that pembrolizumab’s unadjusted association differs materially by poor ECOG; R20 similarly provides no material difference by high NLR; and R21 does not support a material ECOG-by-NLR interaction. These are unadjusted descriptive comparisons and remain vulnerable to allocation, selection, coding, and residual confounding, but their precise near-null estimates do not support continued investigation of effect modification. No additional validation is warranted; validation capacity is better reserved for the anomalous large high-NLR association within stage IV (H14).

All three unadjusted stage-IV interaction estimates are near null, with 95% intervals spanning zero and entirely below the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% clinically significant relative difference. Thus R19-R21 do not support clinically meaningful pembrolizumab effect modification by poor ECOG or high NLR, nor a shared ECOG-by-NLR interaction. These null interaction results do not resolve the striking favorable raw associations in H13-H14: selection, coding, treatment allocation or line/intent, co-treatment, and residual confounding remain plausible competing explanations. I reject H17-H19 as clinically meaningful directional interaction claims rather than interpreting absence of interaction as evidence that the anomalous main effects are biological or causal. Independent replication of H14 remains the most informative next action because it tests whether the second large anomalous descriptive reversal persists.
chair_narrative: R19-R21 provide precise, near-null unadjusted stage-IV interaction estimates. Each 95% interval lies well below the 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a clinically meaningful positive interaction, so there is no support for pembrolizumab effect modification by poor ECOG or high NLR, or for an ECOG-by-NLR interaction. These results are descriptive and do not establish treatment effects or resolve the anomalous favorable raw associations in H13-H14; selection, treatment allocation or line/intent, coding, co-treatment, and residual confounding remain plausible competing explanations. I reject the interaction claims rather than infer that the anomalous main effects are causal or biological. Independent replication of H14 is the most informative next step.

peer_narratives: I propose targeted-treatment contrasts within their molecularly defined stage-IV populations, expecting longer PFS with treatment, and stage-IV EGFR and KRAS-G12C prognostic contrasts to characterize treatment-linked case mix. Effects of at least 0.095 log-months would be clinically material. These unadjusted comparisons remain vulnerable to indication, treatment line, access, and other allocation confounding. To probe the anomalous favorable associations in H13/H14, I also test whether poor ECOG or high NLR is associated with a comparatively worse pembrolizumab contrast; the biological expectation is negative interaction. A null or reversed interaction would instead be compatible with selection, coding, treatment-intent, or residual-confounding explanations rather than protective poor-risk biology.

I propose treatment-effect-modification analyses for the two replicated or strongly supported anomalous stage-IV descriptive associations, plus an ECOG-by-NLR interaction. A clinically material interaction is at least 0.095 log-PFS (approximately a 10% relative PFS difference). The pembrolizumab interactions test whether treatment allocation or treatment-intent mechanisms plausibly contribute to the favorable raw associations of poor ECOG or high NLR. The ECOG-by-NLR interaction tests whether the two reversals cluster in a common patient-selection stratum. Directions are registered as favorable interaction contrasts, but anticipated directions are uncertain: no existing evidence establishes true effect modification. Null interactions would not refute confounding, while clinically material interactions would remain descriptive and compatible with treatment allocation, line of therapy, coding, or residual prognostic confounding rather than biological benefit.
chair_narrative: I prioritize descriptive interaction tests for mechanisms underlying the large, clinically material but implausible favorable stage-IV associations of poor ECOG and high NLR (H13/H14). Pembrolizumab-by-marker interactions test whether treatment allocation, treatment intent, or line-of-therapy selection could contribute; the ECOG-by-NLR interaction tests whether both reversals concentrate in a shared selection stratum. A positive interaction of at least 0.095 log-PFS would be clinically material, but directions are deliberately anticipated as uncertain because existing evidence establishes neither true effect modification nor benefit from poor-risk markers. The drafts’ alternative parameterizations of ECOG-by-pembrolizumab represent the same binary interaction; I retain pembrolizumab as exposure because it makes the treatment-effect-modification question clearer. All results remain unadjusted descriptive associations, with coding, selection, treatment allocation, and residual confounding plausible alternatives.

peer_narratives: H9 is rejected: independent validation R13 precisely reproduces a large association opposite to the original hypothesized detrimental ECOG effect. H14 is accepted as a reproducible unadjusted descriptive association: in stage-IV disease, NLR >=3 is associated with approximately 0.45 higher log-PFS in discovery and validation (R15, R22), greatly exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% clinical difference. This supports the observed association, not a protective, causal, or prognostic interpretation of high NLR. The direction is clinically anomalous and remains vulnerable to selection, coding, treatment allocation or line/intent, co-treatment, and residual confounding. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified descriptive test of whether this anomalous NLR association is modified by a plausible treatment or allocation variable, while recognizing that such interactions cannot establish causality.

H14 is supported as a reproducible, clinically material unadjusted descriptive association: among stage-IV patients, NLR >=3 corresponded to approximately 0.45 higher log-PFS in discovery and validation (R15, R22), greatly exceeding the 0.095 log-PFS clinical-materiality threshold. H9 is rejected because its original hypothesis predicted worse PFS with ECOG PS >=2, whereas both discovery and validation show the opposite raw association (R9, R13). The analogous stage-IV ECOG reversal remains similarly reproducible, but neither result supports a protective, causal, or biologically favorable role for poor ECOG or high NLR. The near-null ECOG-by-NLR and pembrolizumab interaction results do not support a shared effect-modification explanation. Selection, coding, treatment allocation, line/intent, co-treatment, and residual confounding remain unresolved. The most informative next analysis is a preregistered stage-IV interaction analysis testing whether the anomalous ECOG and NLR associations differ by histology, which could assess whether disease-composition heterogeneity plausibly contributes without reinterpreting these raw associations causally.

peer_narratives: H13 is accepted and closed as a robust descriptive finding: among stage-IV patients, ECOG PS >=2 is associated with substantially higher—not lower—log-PFS, with concordant discovery and independent validation estimates of 0.449 and 0.461 log-months (R14, R18). This is far above the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold corresponding to a 10% outcome difference. The result directly contradicts conventional adverse-prognosis expectations, so it does not support a protective biological or causal interpretation of poor performance status. The supported conclusion is limited to a large reproducible unadjusted association. Prior histology and pembrolizumab interaction tests were near null, leaving its mechanism unresolved. Selection or conditioning, coding, treatment allocation/line or intent, co-treatment, and residual confounding remain plausible explanations. The most informative next analysis is whether this anomalous ECOG association differs by high CRP, a marker that itself shows the expected adverse association; this can identify clinically discordant strata but remains noncausal.

H13 is accepted as a reproducible, clinically material descriptive association: among stage-IV patients, ECOG PS >=2 has about 0.46 higher log-PFS than lower ECOG in both discovery and independent validation (R14, R18). This greatly exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold corresponding to a 10% relative outcome difference. The direction is counterintuitive and should not be interpreted as ECOG impairment being beneficial or prognostic after adjustment; selection, treatment allocation, treatment intent/line, coding, co-treatment, and residual confounding remain unresolved. The most informative next analysis is whether this raw reversal differs by EGFR mutation status, a plausible proxy for molecular composition and targeted-treatment allocation. A null result would narrow one potential explanation but still would not establish causality.

peer_narratives: H14 remains accepted and closed: the favorable raw association of high NLR with log-PFS in stage-IV disease reproduced independently (R15, R22; signed validation estimate 0.448, interval 0.434 to 0.461), far exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold corresponding to a 10% relative outcome difference. The most informative next descriptive analysis is whether the anomalous NLR association differs by high CRP status within stage-IV disease; this tests whether the reversal is concentrated in a clinically related inflammatory stratum, while still not resolving causality.

Reject both interactions. H28 is essentially null (R32), and H29 is small and opposite the signed hypothesis (R33). Their 95% intervals lie far within the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold corresponding to a 10% clinically significant relative difference. In addition to lacking clinical importance, these are unadjusted treatment-allocation interactions assessed amid extensive exploratory multiplicity; indication, treatment line/intent, disease severity, co-treatment, molecular composition, and residual confounding remain plausible competing explanations. No independent validation is warranted for near-null findings.
chair_narrative: Reject and close both newly delivered exploratory interactions. H28 is essentially null (0.003 log-PFS; R32), while H29 is small and opposite its signed hypothesis (-0.009; R33). Their 95% intervals are far within the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold corresponding to a clinically significant 10% relative difference. Further, these unadjusted treatment-allocation interactions remain vulnerable to indication, line/intent, disease severity, molecular composition, co-treatment, coding, and residual confounding, so even a nominal small signal would not establish biological effect modification.

peer_narratives: I propose indication-enriched treatment-versus-no-treatment contrasts rather than further biomarker interaction screening. Prior molecular and PD-L1 interaction estimates were small (R1, R2, R4), which argues against clinically important predictive heterogeneity, but does not answer whether the treated group has a clinically material raw PFS difference within the biologically relevant population. A favorable effect of at least about 0.095 log-PFS would meet the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. These are explicitly descriptive comparisons: treatment allocation, line/intent, co-treatment, molecular composition, and prognosis-based selection are plausible alternatives to a pharmacologic benefit. Active H28 should remain the focused test of whether sotorasib allocation explains the anomalous NLR association.

In stage-IV disease, test whether the pembrolizumab versus no-pembrolizumab raw PFS contrast is smaller among patients with CRP >=10 mg/L than among those with lower CRP. The expected direction is negative, consistent with systemic inflammation marking an immunologically adverse state, but this remains unresolved. A magnitude of roughly 0.095 log-PFS or greater would meet the 10% clinical-significance benchmark. Plausible alternatives include treatment allocation, treatment line or intent, disease burden, co-treatment, molecular composition, measurement/coding differences, and residual confounding; thus any result would be descriptive rather than evidence of predictive biology.
chair_narrative: I prioritize the CRP-by-pembrolizumab interaction: among stage-IV patients, the raw pembrolizumab contrast is hypothesized to be smaller with CRP >=10 mg/L, consistent with systemic inflammation as a plausible adverse immunotherapy context. A signed interaction of about 0.095 log-PFS or greater would be clinically material. The alternative explanation is nonrandom treatment allocation, line/intent, disease burden, co-treatment, molecular composition, coding, or residual confounding; this is descriptive rather than causal. I did not adopt the peer's indication-enriched raw treatment-versus-no-treatment comparisons because they primarily reintroduce treatment-selection contrasts after prior treatment-biomarker interactions were clinically small. The CRP interaction is a more specific, falsifiable refinement and complements active H28, which addresses the separate sotorasib–NLR anomaly.

peer_narratives: H10 remains accepted and closed. Discovery and independent validation consistently show that CRP >=10 mg/L is associated with lower log-PFS (signed estimates 0.455 and 0.454; R10, R29). The validation interval remains far from the null and the magnitude substantially exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% relative difference. This is a robust descriptive prognostic association, not evidence that CRP itself causally reduces PFS: inflammation may proxy disease burden, treatment allocation, comorbidity, or other unmeasured factors. Negative findings across the ledger indicate no clinically important treatment-by-biomarker interaction identified so far. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified adjusted prognostic analysis of CRP and NLR jointly with stage, ECOG, age, histology, molecular markers, and treatment assignment, followed by independent validation; this would test whether the striking unadjusted associations reflect independent prognostic information rather than shared confounding.

H10 is supported as a robust descriptive association: high CRP is associated with lower PFS, with discovery and independent validation estimates near 0.454 log-PFS in the adverse signed direction (R10, R29). This greatly exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% relative difference. It remains non-causal because CRP can proxy disease burden, treatment allocation, line/intent, co-treatment, and other unmeasured factors. Negative findings remain the clinically small biomarker-treatment and prognostic-factor interactions, including H28 and H29. The most informative next analysis is whether the anomalous, replicated favorable high-NLR association (H14) persists within stage-IV sotorasib recipients; this probes its dependence on a clinically relevant treatment-allocation stratum, while remaining explicitly descriptive.
chair_narrative: H10 remains accepted and closed. Discovery and independent validation consistently support a large adverse descriptive association of CRP >=10 mg/L with log-PFS (signed estimates 0.455 and 0.454; R10, R29); the validation interval is well beyond the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% relative difference. This is prognostic association evidence, not evidence that CRP causally worsens PFS, because inflammation may proxy disease burden, treatment allocation, line or intent, comorbidity, co-treatment, and other unmeasured factors. Supported findings also include the independently replicated, but biologically counterintuitive, favorable high-NLR association in stage-IV disease (H14; R15, R22). Negative findings include clinically small or null treatment-biomarker and prognostic-factor interactions, including NLR-by-sotorasib (H28; R32) and CRP-by-pembrolizumab (H29; R33). The proposed sotorasib-stratified NLR analysis is the most informative next descriptive check: the near-null H28 interaction suggests the anomalous NLR association may not be treatment-specific, while the within-sotorasib estimate will establish whether its magnitude persists in that clinically relevant allocation stratum. It cannot resolve confounding or establish a causal NLR effect.

peer_narratives: Run the two active, preregistered descriptive contrasts within stage-IV patients allocated sotorasib: H30 for NLR >=3 versus <3 and H31 for CRP >=10 versus <10 mg/L. Use unadjusted Welch mean differences with 95% intervals and two-cell sample-size diagnostics. Judge clinical importance against approximately 0.095 log-PFS (ln[1.10]), while recognizing that allocation-stratified associations remain susceptible to confounding by indication, line/intent, disease burden, molecular composition, co-treatment, and residual factors.

Analyze both active, preregistered sotorasib-stratified prognostic comparisons using unadjusted Welch mean differences and 95% intervals. H30 tests whether the large favorable descriptive high-NLR association persists among stage-IV sotorasib recipients; H31 tests whether elevated CRP retains its adverse descriptive association in the same allocation stratum. Judge magnitude against 0.095 log-PFS (ln[1.10]), the 10% clinical-significance threshold, and verify both exposure-cell counts are at least 20. These are descriptive associations only: selection into sotorasib, treatment line/intent, disease burden, molecular profile, co-treatment, coding, and residual confounding preclude causal or biomarker-effect conclusions.
chair_narrative: Run both active preregistered descriptive contrasts among stage-IV sotorasib recipients: H30 (NLR >=3 versus <3) and H31 (CRP >=10 versus <10 mg/L). Use unadjusted Welch mean differences in log-PFS with 95% intervals and verify both comparison cells have at least 20 observations.
