peer_narratives: Both valid, adequately sized Welch contrasts show very large descriptive associations: high NLR among stage-IV sotorasib recipients has higher log-PFS (H30; R34), while CRP >=10 mg/L has lower log-PFS (H31; R35). Each estimate (~0.45 log units) is far beyond the ~0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. H30 is counterintuitive and should receive independent validation before further interpretation. H31 coheres with the already validated broader CRP association, but neither result supports causal or biomarker-specific conclusions: treatment allocation, disease severity, line/intent, molecular composition, co-treatment, residual confounding, and possible outcome/variable construction or coding artifacts remain plausible explanations. The strikingly similar large effects across several prognostic variables especially warrants caution.

Both contrasts are precise and far exceed the approximately 0.095 log-PFS threshold for a 10% relative difference. H30 shows a large favorable descriptive association for NLR >=3 within stage-IV sotorasib recipients (R34), consistent with the previously replicated counterintuitive stage-IV NLR pattern and the near-null NLR-by-sotorasib interaction. H31 shows a large adverse raw association for CRP >=10 mg/L in the same allocation stratum (R35), consistent with the broader CRP findings. These are unadjusted, noncausal associations and may reflect prognosis-related selection into treatment, disease burden, treatment line/intent, co-treatments, molecular composition, measurement/coding, and residual confounding; they do not support biomarker causality or treatment benefit modification. Given the extensive exploratory multiplicity, no further mechanistic refinement is warranted now.
chair_narrative: Accept both as precise, clinically large descriptive associations: within stage-IV sotorasib recipients, high NLR is associated with higher log-PFS (H30, R34) and CRP >=10 mg/L with lower log-PFS (H31, R35). Each estimate is about 0.45 log units, far exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. H30 is counterintuitive but is compatible with the previously replicated stage-IV NLR pattern and the near-null NLR-by-sotorasib interaction; H31 is consistent with the broader and stage-IV CRP findings. I close both rather than request validation because they are exploratory allocation-stratified descriptive duplicates/refinements and further replication would not address their central limitations. The strikingly similar large effects across several prognostic variables raises concern for shared construction, coding, selection, or confounding mechanisms. These unadjusted contrasts cannot establish biomarker causality, treatment benefit, or effect modification; disease burden, treatment line/intent, treatment allocation, molecular composition, co-treatments, comorbidity, measurement artifacts, and residual confounding remain plausible competing explanations.

peer_narratives: Propose testing whether the large adverse descriptive association of CRP >=10 mg/L with PFS persists among stage-IV patients allocated sotorasib. H10 and the stage-IV refinement H16 support an adverse association overall, whereas H30 will separately assess the anomalous NLR pattern in this same treatment stratum. A signed effect of at least about 0.095 log-PFS would meet the prespecified 10% clinical-significance threshold. This is a prognostic descriptive comparison, not causal evidence: inflammatory burden may proxy disease severity, treatment line or intent, molecular composition, co-treatment, comorbidity, and residual confounding.

I propose direction-reversed refinements of H12 and H9 to formally characterize the highly counterintuitive raw associations suggested by their evidence: high NLR and ECOG >=2 each appear associated with longer, rather than shorter, log-PFS in the full cohort. The approximately 0.45-log-unit raw contrasts implied by R12 and R9/R13 are far larger than the 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference, but these revisions are exploratory and should not be interpreted as protective biological effects. Plausible alternatives include treatment allocation and indication, line or intent, disease-burden selection, measurement or coding artifacts, survivor/conditioning bias, co-treatment, and unmeasured clinical or molecular confounding. H30 remains the most useful immediate check of whether the paradoxical NLR association persists within sotorasib-treated stage-IV patients.
chair_narrative: Test whether the large adverse descriptive association of CRP >=10 mg/L with PFS persists among stage-IV patients receiving sotorasib. This focused refinement complements active H30 and assesses inflammatory prognostic stratification within the same clinically relevant treatment allocation; an absolute signed contrast of roughly 0.095 log-PFS or more would meet the 10% clinical-significance threshold. I did not adopt direction-reversed full-cohort ECOG or NLR proposals: their counterintuitive raw patterns are already more informatively established in stage-IV refinements H13 and H14, including validation, and re-registering broad reversals would add little. Any association here remains noncausal and may reflect disease burden, treatment line or intent, selection into sotorasib, molecular composition, co-treatment, comorbidity, coding, or residual confounding.

peer_narratives: No new validation result or response deadline is listed for this synthesis stage. Supported findings remain large descriptive prognostic associations: high CRP is associated with lower PFS overall and in stage-IV disease, with independent validation of the overall result (H10; R10, R29), while high NLR and ECOG >=2 show counterintuitive higher-PFS associations in stage-IV disease, with NLR independently replicated (H14; R15, R22) and ECOG independently replicated (H13; R14, R18). The roughly 0.45-log-unit magnitudes imply differences far above the 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative outcome difference. These are associations only and cannot establish causal biomarker effects or treatment benefit. Negative findings include treatment-biomarker interactions that are near zero and well below clinical importance, including NLR-by-sotorasib (H28; R32) and CRP-by-pembrolizumab (H29; R33). The highly repetitive, unusually large prognostic contrasts leave unresolved concern about shared construction, coding, selection, or residual-confounding mechanisms. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified negative-control association using constructed research marker D: a similarly large association without a defined biological role would strengthen concern that the observed prognostic pattern is not clinically interpretable; a null result would not remove confounding concerns but would be somewhat reassuring.

Supported findings remain descriptive rather than causal. Elevated CRP is consistently associated with substantially shorter PFS overall and in stage-IV disease (H10, H16), including independent validation for H10 (R10, R29); its approximately 0.45 log-unit magnitude greatly exceeds the 0.095 log-unit threshold corresponding to a 10% relative difference. Within stage-IV sotorasib recipients, the same adverse CRP association is also large (H31, R35). Conversely, high NLR is associated with longer PFS in stage-IV disease, independently replicated in H14 (R15, R22), and similarly within sotorasib recipients (H30, R34); this counterintuitive pattern should not be interpreted as a protective biological effect.

Negative findings are informative: treatment-biomarker interactions were generally near null and far below clinical importance, including NLR-by-sotorasib (H28, R32), CRP-by-pembrolizumab (H29, R33), and NLR-by-CRP (H26, R30). Thus, the large prognostic associations do not presently identify a treatment-predictive biomarker.

Key uncertainty is whether the repeated, unusually similar large prognostic contrasts reflect disease severity, treatment line/intent and allocation, correlated unmeasured clinical factors, coding or construction artifacts, or other confounding. The most informative next analysis is a preregistered CRP-by-sotorasib interaction in stage-IV disease. It tests whether the adverse CRP association is materially altered by sotorasib allocation; given R17 and R35, a null result would support descriptive consistency across that allocation while still not establishing causality.
chair_narrative: No validation result or response deadline is due. Supported findings remain large descriptive prognostic associations: CRP >=10 mg/L is associated with shorter PFS overall with independent validation (H10; R10, R29), while higher NLR and ECOG >=2 are associated with longer PFS in stage-IV disease, including independent validation (H14, R15, R22; H13, R14, R18). These approximately 0.45-log-unit contrasts greatly exceed the 0.095-log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference, but are not causal biomarker effects or treatment-benefit evidence. Negative findings are the clinically small treatment-biomarker interactions, including NLR-by-sotorasib (H28; R32), CRP-by-pembrolizumab (H29; R33), and NLR-by-CRP (H26; R30), whose intervals remain below the clinical-importance threshold. I favor a constructed-marker negative-control analysis over the proposed CRP-by-sotorasib interaction: H16, H31, and the existing near-null interaction pattern already make another allocation-stratified interaction less diagnostic of the striking repeated prognostic pattern. A large association for research marker D, which has no assigned clinical role, would materially heighten concern about shared construction, coding, selection, or residual-confounding artifacts; a null result would be somewhat reassuring but would not establish causality for the observed biomarker associations.

peer_narratives: Run the three preregistered full-cohort unadjusted Welch contrasts for constructed research markers D, E, and F versus their negative counterparts (H32–H34), checking both cells exceed 20 observations. These have no assigned biological or clinical role and serve as negative-control probes of the striking repeated approximately 0.45-log-PFS prognostic associations. Interpret absolute effects against 0.095 log-PFS (ln[1.10]), the 10% clinical-significance threshold. Concordant clinically large marker associations would support concern about shared construction, selection, coding, or residual-confounding artifacts; null or clinically trivial effects would be reassuring but would not establish causal interpretations for CRP, NLR, ECOG, or treatment findings.

Run the three prespecified full-cohort constructed-marker negative-control contrasts (H32–H34). Estimate unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS differences using Welch 95% intervals and confirm both cells exceed 20 observations. Interpret absolute effects >=0.095 log-PFS (ln[1.10]) as clinically large descriptively. Because markers D–F have no assigned biological or clinical role, concordant large associations would be evidence of possible shared construction, selection, coding, or residual-confounding artifacts underlying the repetitive prognostic associations; null or clinically trivial results would be only limited reassurance and would not establish causality for CRP, NLR, or ECOG.
chair_narrative: Run the three prespecified full-cohort constructed-marker negative-control contrasts (H32–H34): unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS differences with Welch 95% intervals, confirming both cells exceed 20 observations. Marker D, E, and F have no assigned biological or clinical role. Interpret an absolute contrast of at least 0.095 log-PFS (ln[1.10]) as clinically large descriptively. Concordant large effects would increase concern that the repeated approximately 0.45-log-PFS prognostic associations reflect shared construction, coding, selection, or residual confounding; null or clinically trivial controls would provide only limited reassurance and would not establish causal interpretations for CRP, NLR, ECOG, or treatments.

peer_narratives: Research marker D shows a precise +0.151 log-PFS association (R36), corresponding to roughly a 16% relative difference and exceeding the 10% clinical-significance threshold descriptively. I accept the association as a reproducible-to-be-tested descriptive finding, not as biomarker biology or causal evidence: the marker has no assigned role, and its large association strengthens concern about constructed-variable artifacts, selection, shared data-generating structure, or residual confounding behind the repetitive prognostic effects. Markers E and F are clinically trivial and their intervals exclude a 10% relative difference (R37, R38), so their positive-association claims are rejected. The discordance among the three controls makes a universal shared artifact less likely but does not rescue causal interpretation of D or prior prognostic associations.

H32 shows a precise, clinically large positive descriptive association (0.151 log-PFS; 95% CI 0.142 to 0.160), exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-unit 10% clinical-significance threshold. Because marker D has no assigned biological or clinical role, this result is chiefly a negative-control warning rather than evidence of a meaningful biomarker: it materially strengthens concerns that the repeated large unadjusted prognostic contrasts reflect shared data construction, coding/selection artifacts, disease-burden imbalance, or residual confounding. Independent replication is useful to distinguish a split-specific anomaly from a reproducible structural artifact, although replication would not make the association causal or biologically interpretable. H33 and H34 are precise clinically trivial/null contrasts, with intervals far below the clinical threshold; together they show that the concern is not simply universal association across every constructed marker, but they do not resolve the explanation for H32 or for CRP, NLR, and ECOG findings.
chair_narrative: H32 is accepted only as a precise, clinically large descriptive association: marker-D positivity is associated with +0.151 log-PFS (R36), exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. Because D has no assigned biological or clinical role, this is not biomarker or causal evidence; rather, it is an important negative-control warning of possible shared construction, coding, selection, or residual-confounding mechanisms underlying the repetitive prognostic contrasts. Independent validation is warranted to distinguish a split-specific result from a reproducible structural artifact, without conferring biological interpretation. H33 and H34 are rejected as clinically meaningful positive associations: their intervals are tightly far below the clinical-significance threshold. Their null/trivial results make a universal association across every constructed marker less likely, but do not resolve the explanation for marker D or prior CRP, NLR, and ECOG associations. The participant drafts agreed substantively; I retain this interpretation while emphasizing multiplicity and the noncausal role of the negative-control finding.

peer_narratives: Alongside active H32, I propose markers E and F as prespecified constructed-marker negative controls in the full cohort. No biological direction is expected; estimates of either sign are plausible. A clinically large association (absolute log-PFS contrast about 0.095 or greater, corresponding to 10%) for multiple markers with no assigned clinical role would strengthen concern that the repeated large prognostic contrasts reflect shared construction, coding, selection, or residual confounding rather than interpretable biomarker biology. Null or clinically trivial contrasts would be reassuring about this particular artifact hypothesis, but would not establish causality for the observed CRP, NLR, or ECOG associations. The next analysis should include H32 and these two independent negative-control contrasts, with valid cell sizes and 95% Welch intervals.

I propose two prespecified constructed-assay negative controls, marker E and marker F positivity versus negativity in the full cohort. Their expected raw contrasts are uncertain because these assays have no assigned biological or clinical role. Results of at least 0.095 log-PFS units (approximately a 10% relative difference) would be clinically large descriptively, but would not support biomarker causality. Concordant large associations across these unassigned markers and active H32 would instead strengthen concern that the repeated approximately 0.45-log-unit prognostic contrasts reflect shared outcome construction, coding, selection, disease-burden imbalance, treatment allocation, or residual confounding. Null results would be somewhat reassuring but would not resolve those alternatives for established clinical markers.
chair_narrative: Add research markers E and F as prespecified full-cohort constructed-assay negative controls alongside active H32. These assays have no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role, so no raw direction is anticipated. A contrast of either sign with absolute magnitude at least 0.095 log-PFS units would be clinically large descriptively; concordant large associations across these unassigned markers would heighten concern that the repeated roughly 0.45-log-unit prognostic contrasts arise from shared construction, coding, selection, disease-burden imbalance, treatment allocation, or residual confounding rather than interpretable biomarker biology. Null or clinically trivial control contrasts would be somewhat reassuring about that artifact hypothesis but would not establish causality for CRP, NLR, or ECOG associations. The participant drafts were substantively aligned; I retain both controls because a small panel is more diagnostic than marker D alone.

peer_narratives: H32 is supported as a reproducible descriptive finding: marker-D positivity has a +0.158 log-PFS contrast in independent validation (R39, 99.6% interval 0.145 to 0.171), consistent with discovery R36 and entirely above the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. This establishes neither a causal nor a biological biomarker effect because marker D has no assigned clinical role. Instead, reproducibility makes it a stronger warning that shared data construction, selection, or residual confounding may contribute to the striking prognostic patterns. Marker E and F were null/trivial, so the concern is not a universal artifact across all constructed markers, but the explanation for D remains unresolved. The most informative next analysis is whether the D association persists within stage-IV disease; persistence would make simple imbalance in stage less adequate as an explanation.

H32 is supported as a reproducible descriptive association: research-marker-D positivity is associated with longer log-PFS (+0.158, independent R39 99.6%-level interval 0.145 to 0.171), and even the lower bound exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. This validates the association’s reproducibility, not a biological, prognostic, or causal interpretation, because marker D has no assigned clinical role. The null/trivial E and F controls argue against a universal constructed-marker artifact, but the marker-D result remains an important warning that unmeasured construction, coding, selection, or confounding can generate clinically large associations. The most informative next analysis would be an adjusted or data-generating-structure audit of marker D and the repetitive CRP/NLR/ECOG contrasts; available unadjusted subgroup contrasts cannot distinguish causal clinical effects from structural artifact.
chair_narrative: H32 is supported as a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association: marker-D positivity is associated with longer log-PFS in independent validation (+0.158; R39 interval 0.145 to 0.171), consistent with discovery (R36). Even the validation lower bound exceeds the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. This does not establish a biological, prognostic, or causal biomarker effect because marker D has no assigned clinical role. Instead, its reproducibility makes it a strong warning that shared data construction, selection, coding, or residual confounding may produce striking prognostic patterns. The null/trivial E and F controls argue against an artifact affecting every constructed marker, but do not explain D. I retain active investigation and add the stage-IV refinement as the most informative available next analysis: persistence within stage-IV disease would make simple stage imbalance an inadequate explanation, while attenuation would identify stage composition as a plausible contributor. The drafts agree on descriptive acceptance; I favor active rather than closed investigation because this prespecified refinement directly addresses a major unresolved structural explanation.

peer_narratives: Analyze the prespecified stage-stratified marker-D negative-control contrasts (H35–H37) using unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS and Welch 95% intervals. Interpret an absolute effect of approximately 0.095 log units (ln[1.10]) or more as clinically large descriptively. Comparing H35 and H36 will test whether the reproducible full-cohort marker-D association (R36, R39) persists within both stage strata; H37 directly quantifies heterogeneity. These are diagnostics of data structure, stage composition, selection, or residual confounding—not evidence of a biological or causal role for the unassigned constructed marker. Require all comparison cells to meet the stated minimum and treat intervals spanning the clinical threshold as uncertain even if statistically non-null.

Analyze the prespecified marker-D stratified contrasts: within stage-IV (H35), within non-stage-IV (H36), and their formal stage-IV interaction (H37). Each is an unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS contrast estimated with Welch 95% intervals; all expected cells are well above the 20-observation minimum. The clinically meaningful threshold is approximately 0.095 log units (ln[1.10]). No new effect estimates, uncertainty intervals, or diagnostics are yet available in this stage. The key diagnostic is concordance of H35 and H36 versus a clinically meaningful H37 interaction: similar large effects would rule out simple stage-composition imbalance as the sole explanation for the reproducible but non-biological marker-D association (R36, R39), whereas attenuation in either stratum or a large interaction would support stage-linked construction, selection, or confounding. The prior null/trivial marker-E and marker-F findings (R37–R38) remain relevant negative findings but do not explain marker D.
chair_narrative: Run the prespecified marker-D stratified negative-control contrasts: within stage-IV disease (H35), within non-stage-IV disease (H36), and their formal stage interaction (H37). Estimate unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS differences using Welch 95% intervals; each cell must meet the 20-observation minimum. A magnitude of 0.095 log units (ln[1.10]) or greater is clinically large descriptively. Concordant large within-stratum associations would show that simple stage composition alone cannot explain the reproducible full-cohort marker-D association (R36, R39), whereas attenuation or a clinically meaningful interaction would support stage-linked construction, selection, or residual confounding. Since marker D has no assigned biological or clinical role, none of these analyses can establish a biomarker or causal effect.

peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has clinically large descriptive associations with longer log-PFS within both stage-IV disease (H35, +0.151; 95% CI 0.141 to 0.162) and non-stage-IV disease (H36, +0.143; 0.129 to 0.157). Both lower bounds exceed the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold corresponding to a 10% relative difference. The stage interaction is small and imprecise around zero (H37, +0.008; -0.009 to +0.025), and its interval excludes clinically important stage-specific heterogeneity; simple stage composition is therefore not an adequate explanation for the marker-D association. These are nevertheless unadjusted observational contrasts for a constructed marker with no assigned biological role, selected amid multiple exploratory comparisons. They support a reproducible data-structure/negative-control warning, not a causal, prognostic-biomarker, or treatment-guiding conclusion. Residual confounding, selection, or shared outcome/assay construction remain plausible competing explanations.

Marker-D positivity has a clinically large descriptive association with longer PFS in both stage-IV (+0.151 log-months, R40) and non-stage-IV disease (+0.143, R41); both interval lower bounds exceed the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference. The negligible stage interaction (+0.008, R42; interval -0.009 to +0.025) excludes clinically important stage heterogeneity, so simple stage composition is not an adequate explanation. However, these are unadjusted, post-discovery stratified comparisons with nominal intervals and substantial multiplicity. As D is an unassigned constructed assay, the replicated pattern remains descriptive only and is compatible with leakage, shared construction, selection, or residual confounding; it does not support a biological, prognostic, or causal biomarker interpretation.
chair_narrative: Marker-D positivity has clinically large descriptive associations with longer log-PFS within both stage-IV disease (H35: +0.151, R40) and non-stage-IV disease (H36: +0.143, R41); both 95% interval lower bounds exceed approximately 0.095 log units, the 10% relative-difference threshold. The stage interaction is trivial (+0.008, R42; -0.009 to +0.025) and excludes clinically important heterogeneity in either direction, so stage composition alone is not an adequate explanation for the marker-D association. However, these are unadjusted, post-discovery stratified observational contrasts with nominal intervals and substantial exploratory multiplicity. As D is an unassigned constructed assay, the findings support a reproducible data-structure/negative-control warning rather than a biological, prognostic, causal, or treatment-guiding interpretation; leakage, shared construction, selection, and residual confounding remain plausible competing explanations. The participant drafts agree substantively; I retain active investigation of the descriptive pattern and request validation of the stage-IV result.

peer_narratives: H35 should remain the immediate within-stage-IV follow-up for the reproducible but biologically uninterpretable marker-D association. I additionally propose the stage-IV interaction as a falsifiable refinement: it tests whether the marker-D prognostic contrast differs by metastatic stage, rather than merely documenting persistence in one stage stratum. No direction is predicted because marker D has no assigned biology. A clinically meaningful interaction would require roughly 0.095 log-PFS units (about a 10% relative difference); a trivial, precise interaction would argue against stage composition as the principal explanation for the marker-D association, while a large interaction would make stage-linked construction or selection a plausible alternative.

I propose the non-stage-IV counterpart to active H35. In patients without stage-IV disease, marker-D positivity versus negativity is expected to have uncertain raw direction because D lacks an assigned biological role. Together with H35, this falsifiably tests whether the reproducible full-cohort +0.158 log-PFS association (R39; also R36) persists across stage strata. Concordant clinically large effects (at least about 0.095 log units) would argue against simple stage composition as its sole explanation, although not against shared construction or residual confounding. Attenuation to clinically trivial effects in both strata would support stage mixing as a plausible explanation; a large effect confined to one stratum would suggest effect heterogeneity or a stratum-specific artifact.
chair_narrative: Retain active H35 and add its non-stage-IV counterpart plus the direct stage-IV interaction. Marker D’s reproducible full-cohort association is clinically large descriptively (+0.158 log-PFS in validation, R39; lower bound exceeds 0.095), but has no biological interpretation because D is an unassigned constructed assay. Persistence of a clinically large association in both strata would make stage composition alone inadequate, whereas attenuation or a clinically meaningful interaction (about 0.095 log units or more) would support stage-linked construction, selection, or confounding as a plausible explanation. The drafts differed only in emphasis: the non-stage-IV comparison is needed to interpret the existing within-stage-IV result, while the interaction is the most direct falsifiable heterogeneity test; both are retained.

peer_narratives: H35 is supported as a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association within stage-IV disease: independent validation estimates marker-D positivity at +0.151 log-PFS (R43, 0.136 to 0.166), with the entire interval exceeding the approximately 0.095 log-unit threshold for a 10% relative difference and agreeing with discovery (R40). The previously observed near-null stage interaction (R42) provides no evidence that this association is stage-specific. This is not evidence that marker D is a biological, prognostic, causal, or treatment-guiding biomarker: D is an unassigned constructed assay and all contrasts are unadjusted, leaving shared construction, selection, leakage, and residual confounding unresolved. The null E and F findings remain useful negative controls but cannot exclude a D-specific artifact. The most informative next action is independent validation of the non-stage-IV marker-D contrast (H36), which would test whether the clinically large descriptive pattern persists outside stage-IV disease under the same stringent validation framework.

H35 is supported as a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association: within stage-IV disease, marker-D positivity is associated with longer log-PFS in discovery (+0.151, R40) and independent validation (+0.151, R43; interval +0.136 to +0.166). The validation lower bound exceeds ln(1.10)≈0.095, so the association remains clinically significant by the prespecified threshold. Concordant stage-IV and non-stage-IV estimates (H36/R41), together with the near-null stage interaction (H37/R42), indicate that simple stage composition does not explain the signal. Nonetheless, marker D is a constructed assay without assigned biological or clinical meaning, and these are unadjusted observational contrasts. The supported conclusion is therefore a reproducible data-structure/negative-control warning, not a prognostic biomarker, causal effect, or treatment-selection finding. Residual confounding, selection, leakage, or shared outcome-related construction remain unresolved. The most informative next action is independent validation of the non-stage-IV marker-D association (H36), which would test whether the clinically large descriptive pattern persists across both stage strata under the stringent validation framework.

Marker D has a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association with longer PFS overall and within stage strata (R39–R43), but its constructed, unassigned nature makes residual baseline-risk structure or outcome-linked construction more plausible than biomarker biology. ECOG ≥2 is a clinically meaningful severity stratum with a large observed prognostic contrast (R9, R13). The next useful falsification is therefore to estimate the D association separately by ECOG status and formally test heterogeneity. Persistence of a >=ln(1.10) association in both strata with a clinically trivial interaction would further argue against simple performance-status composition as the explanation, while marked attenuation in either stratum or an interaction of roughly 0.095 log units or greater would support confounding, selection, or construction-related explanations. These analyses remain descriptive and cannot establish clinical utility or causality.

peer_narratives: H32 is supported as a reproducible descriptive association: marker-D positivity is associated with longer log-PFS in discovery (R36, +0.151) and validation (R39, +0.158; 99.6% interval +0.145 to +0.171). Negative findings include no meaningful associations for markers E or F and no clinically important stage heterogeneity for marker D. These findings remain unadjusted observational associations, not evidence of a causal, biological, prognostic, or treatment-selecting biomarker role: D is an unassigned constructed assay, and D-specific construction artifact, leakage, selection, and residual confounding remain unresolved. The most informative next analysis is to test whether marker-D association differs by a clinically actionable treatment exposure, preferably a prespecified treatment interaction, rather than conduct further broad marker or subgroup searches.

H32 and H36 are supported as reproducible descriptive associations: marker-D positivity is associated with longer PFS overall (R36/R39) and in non-stage-IV disease (R41/R44). The most informative next analysis, if supported by the controller, would be a prespecified confounder-adjusted and leakage-audited external evaluation of marker D rather than another unadjusted stratification.
chair_narrative: H32 and H36 are supported as reproducible descriptive associations: marker-D positivity is associated with longer log-PFS overall (R36, R39) and among non-stage-IV patients (R41, R44). The validation lower bounds, +0.145 overall and +0.127 in non-stage-IV disease, exceed ln(1.10)≈0.095, supporting clinically meaningful relative differences under the stated threshold. Concordant stage-IV evidence (H35/R40, R43) and the small stage interaction (H37/R42) indicate that stage composition is not an adequate explanation and provide negative evidence for clinically important stage heterogeneity. Markers E and F show no clinically meaningful association, but their null results do not establish D specificity or biological validity. The substantive disagreement between drafts is whether to leave H32/H36 active; because their requested independent validations are now delivered and no further unadjusted subgroup analysis would resolve the central limitations, I close these descriptive claims. They do not support causal, biological prognostic, or treatment-guiding use: D is an unassigned constructed assay and leakage, D-specific construction artifact, selection, and residual confounding remain unresolved. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified leakage-audited, confounder-adjusted external evaluation of D, ideally including a clinically actionable treatment interaction rather than further broad subgroup searches.

peer_narratives: Request the prespecified stage-IV pembrolizumab-by-marker-D interaction (H38). Run H38, the prespecified stage-IV pembrolizumab-by-marker-D interaction. chair_narrative: Request H38, the prespecified stage-IV pembrolizumab-by-marker-D interaction. peer_narratives: H38 shows no evidence that marker-D status modifies pembrolizumab association in stage-IV disease (R45 signed interaction −0.0033, 95% CI −0.0236 to 0.0171; all cells large). The interval excludes an interaction remotely near the clinically meaningful 10% relative threshold (ln[1.10]≈0.095). This unadjusted observational comparison would in any case be vulnerable to treatment-selection confounding and assay-construction artifacts, but neither limitation rescues the proposed clinically meaningful positive interaction. Further validation of this near-null, precise result is not a useful allocation.

R45 provides no evidence that marker-D positivity modifies pembrolizumab association in stage-IV disease: the signed interaction is -0.003 log-months (95% CI -0.024 to 0.017), far below the clinically meaningful threshold of ln(1.10)≈0.095 and with ample cell sizes. This null interaction also argues against treating the reproducible unadjusted marker-D prognostic association as treatment-predictive. As D is an unassigned constructed assay, any clinical or biological interpretation would additionally remain vulnerable to leakage, construction artifact, selection, and confounding; no validation request is warranted for this clearly non-meaningful interaction.
chair_narrative: H38 provides precise negative evidence for clinically meaningful marker-D modification of the pembrolizumab association in stage-IV disease: the signed interaction is -0.0033 log-months (95% CI -0.0236 to 0.0171), far below the 10% threshold of ln(1.10)≈0.095, with all comparison cells large. This unadjusted observational interaction remains susceptible to treatment-selection confounding and constructed-assay artifacts, but those limitations do not support the proposed clinically meaningful positive predictive interaction. peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful descriptive association with longer PFS in stage-IV disease: both R40 and R43 are about +0.15 log-months, and their lower bounds exceed ln(1.10)≈0.095. I therefore accept and close H35 as a descriptive prognostic association, while retaining the important caveat that D is an unassigned constructed assay and this does not establish biological validity or causality. The next focused, falsifiable comparison is whether marker D modifies pembrolizumab-associated PFS in stage-IV disease. A positive interaction would be clinically actionable if it exceeded the 10% relative threshold; however, the anticipated direction is uncertain because the observed prognostic association does not imply treatment prediction, and leakage, assay construction artifact, treatment selection, and residual confounding remain plausible alternatives.

Marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association with longer PFS in stage-IV disease (H35; R40, R43), but the unassigned constructed assay cannot yet be interpreted as biological or clinically actionable. A prespecified stage-IV pembrolizumab-by-marker-D interaction is the most useful next comparison: it tests whether D provides predictive information beyond its prognostic association. I am uncertain about the raw interaction direction because there is no assigned mechanism and prior treatment-biomarker interactions were small; a clinically meaningful positive interaction would require a benefit difference of roughly 0.095 log-months or greater, whereas a null result would argue against treatment-guiding use of D.
chair_narrative: Marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful descriptive association with longer PFS in stage-IV disease: R40 and R43 are approximately +0.15 log-months and their lower bounds exceed ln(1.10) (~0.095). peer_narratives: Analyze the four registered direct treatment-versus-no-treatment contrasts in their matched stage-IV biomarker-defined populations. For each, evaluate the signed Welch mean difference and 95% interval against the clinical threshold ln(1.10)=0.095 log-months, and confirm both cells meet the minimum-size diagnostic. These are descriptive associations, not causal treatment effects: confounding by indication, treatment timing/line, and correlated clinical or molecular selection may materially bias their direction and magnitude. The prior null interaction findings (H1–H4) do not preclude a direct within-biomarker association, but they weigh against interpreting any result as evidence of selective treatment benefit without adjustment or independent evaluation.

Request the four registered direct, biomarker-matched treatment contrasts in stage-IV disease. These address within-selected-population associations that the earlier interaction tests did not estimate. For each, assess the signed exposed-minus-comparator Welch estimate and 95% interval against ln(1.10)=0.095 log-months as the clinical-significance threshold, and verify both cells meet the minimum-size diagnostic. These are unadjusted observational contrasts, so even a clinically large association would remain vulnerable to confounding by indication, treatment line, prognosis, and correlated molecular selection; a near-null result would similarly concern the observed association rather than definitive treatment efficacy.
chair_narrative: Run the four registered direct treatment-versus-no-treatment contrasts within their matched stage-IV biomarker-defined populations (H39–H42). H39 and H40 have upper 95% bounds of 0.052 and 0.056, respectively; H41 is imprecise but its point estimate is negative and its upper bound is only 0.058; and H42 is nominally positive (+0.022) but its upper bound is 0.045. Thus none supports a clinically significant positive association. These are also unadjusted observational contrasts vulnerable to confounding by indication, treatment line, and molecular/prognostic selection; this further precludes efficacy interpretation but does not rescue the proposed meaningful positive effects. No validation is warranted.

peer_narratives: The prior biomarker-treatment interaction results reject clinically meaningful effect modification, but an interaction is not a test of the treatment contrast within the biologically selected population. I therefore propose direct, target-population treatment comparisons for EGFR-mutant/osimertinib, KRAS-G12C/sotorasib, BRCA2-mutant/olaparib, and high-PD-L1/pembrolizumab stage-IV disease. Each predicts longer PFS with treatment; a signed effect of at least ln(1.10) (~0.095 log-months) would meet the clinical-significance criterion. These are falsifiable descriptive associations, not causal efficacy estimates: confounding by indication, treatment line, unmeasured molecular features, and selection into treatment remain plausible alternatives, especially if effects are absent or unexpectedly negative.

Marker-D positivity has a reproducible clinically meaningful descriptive prognostic association (H35), but its unassigned constructed nature makes treatment-predictive use highly uncertain; the pembrolizumab interaction was already precisely null (H38/R45). The most useful remaining falsifiable tests are whether marker D modifies matched targeted-treatment associations in stage-IV molecularly defined populations. I anticipate no consistent raw interaction direction, but register positive interactions because a benefit of at least ln(1.10)≈0.095 log-months would be clinically meaningful. Plausible alternatives for any apparent interaction include treatment-selection confounding, assay construction/leakage, sparse BRCA2-positive treated cells, and chance subgroup variation rather than biological prediction.
chair_narrative: I propose direct treatment-versus-no-treatment contrasts within the biologically matched stage-IV populations. The earlier interaction claims H1–H4 were precisely negative for effect modification, but do not answer whether the treated and untreated groups differ within the intended biomarker-selected population. Each hypothesis predicts longer PFS with the matched treatment; an effect of at least ln(1.10) (~0.095 log-months) is clinically meaningful. I do not pursue further marker-D treatment interactions: H38 was precisely null and D is an unassigned constructed assay, making additional subgroup searches low-value. These direct contrasts remain descriptive observational associations, with confounding by indication, treatment line, co-mutations, and selection into treatment as plausible alternatives to a positive or negative result.

peer_narratives: H36 is supported as a reproducible descriptive association: in non-stage-IV disease, research-marker-D positivity was associated with +0.147 log-months PFS on independent validation (R44, 99.6% interval +0.127 to +0.168). Negative findings include the lack of clinically meaningful biomarker-matched treatment associations (H39-H42), whose upper bounds all remain below +0.095 log-months. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified leakage-audited and confounder-adjusted evaluation of marker D, prioritizing a clinically actionable treatment-interaction endpoint rather than additional unadjusted subgroup searches.

H36 is independently supported: in non-stage-IV disease, research-marker-D positivity was associated with +0.147 log-months PFS in validation (R44), with its multiplicity-adjusted lower bound (+0.127) exceeding ln(1.10)≈0.095. Marker D showed similarly sized associations overall and in stage-IV disease (H32, H35), while no stage-related heterogeneity was demonstrated (H37), reinforcing consistency but not biological interpretation. peer_narratives: H43 and H44 show clinically significant descriptive marker-D associations in stage-IV EGFR-mutant and KRAS-G12C subsets: their lower 95% bounds (0.115 and 0.135 log-months) exceed ln(1.10)≈0.095. H43 and H44 show clinically significant descriptive marker-D associations in stage-IV EGFR-mutant and KRAS-G12C subsets: their lower 95% bounds (+0.115 and +0.135 log-months) exceed ln(1.10)≈0.095. They are consistent with the already replicated overall and stage-specific marker-D findings, but were exploratory subgroup analyses and cannot establish biology, prognosis independent of confounding, causality, or treatment utility. chair_narrative: H43 and H44 support the narrowly descriptive finding that marker-D positivity is associated with longer PFS in the respective stage-IV EGFR-mutant and KRAS-G12C subsets: lower 95% bounds (+0.115 and +0.135 log-months) exceed the clinical benchmark ln(1.10)=0.095. This does not establish molecular-subgroup biomarker portability, biological mechanism, independent prognosis, causality, or treatment utility: marker D is a constructed unassigned assay, and assay construction/leakage, clinical and molecular confounding, treatment selection, and exploratory subgroup multiplicity remain credible alternatives. I retain H43 as active and request independent validation because the EGFR-subgroup-specific conclusion has not itself been independently tested; H44 is closed because it is a concordant exploratory extension rather than a distinct mechanistic signal. H45 is rejected: its interval (-0.045 to +0.008 log-months) excludes a clinically important positive ECOG interaction and is also too small in the opposite direction to indicate material heterogeneity.

peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically large descriptive association with longer PFS overall and in both stage strata (H32, H35, H36), while stage interaction was near null (H37). A useful next question is whether that association is retained in clinically important molecular subsets and whether it differs by poor performance status. I have no biologically grounded directional expectation because marker D is an unassigned constructed assay; all proposals are therefore exploratory and unresolved. Compare the estimate and 95% interval with log(1.10)=0.095, the clinically meaningful relative-PFS threshold. This tests treatment selectivity rather than the replicated descriptive prognostic association of marker D; any result remains observational and vulnerable to treatment allocation, BRCA2-linked heterogeneity, baseline severity/inflammation, molecular co-segregation, and cohort structure.

peer_narratives: H36 is unresolved. The signed marker-D-by-olaparib interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease is 0.082 log-months (95% CI -0.038 to 0.201; R44). Although the estimate is positive, it is below the prespecified clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)=0.095 and the interval includes both no interaction and clinically meaningful benefit. The relatively small treatment-by-marker cells also leave substantial uncertainty. This unadjusted observational interaction remains vulnerable to treatment allocation, BRCA2-linked heterogeneity, molecular co-segregation, baseline severity, and chance; it does not yet support a predictive biomarker claim.

H36 is unresolved. The marker-D-by-olaparib interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease is positive but imprecise (0.082 log-months, 95% CI -0.038 to 0.201; R44). It includes no interaction and clinically meaningful benefit (log[1.10]≈0.095), so neither acceptance nor rejection is justified. Although all cells meet the minimum size, the BRCA2/marker/treatment cells are relatively sparse and this is an exploratory refinement after multiple biomarker analyses. Unadjusted observational contrasts also remain vulnerable to treatment allocation, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, prognostic marker-D effects, and baseline clinical confounding. Independent validation is warranted before treating this as evidence of olaparib selectivity.
chair_narrative: H36 remains unresolved. The signed marker-D-by-olaparib interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease is 0.082 log-months (95% CI -0.038 to 0.201; R44). It is below the clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)=0.095, while its interval includes both no interaction and clinically meaningful benefit. peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has a replicated, clinically meaningful descriptive association with longer PFS overall and in several examined strata (H19, H22, H23, H29, H30, H32), but it has not predicted differential pembrolizumab, osimertinib, or sotorasib associations (H24, H34, H35). A useful remaining falsifiable predictive test is whether marker D modifies the olaparib association specifically among BRCA2-mutant patients. I anticipate uncertainty rather than benefit because the prior treatment interactions were near null; a positive interaction at least log(1.10)=0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Alternatives to a positive result include a purely prognostic marker-D association, treatment allocation, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, baseline severity/inflammation, cohort structure, or chance.

I propose a distinct predictive-biomarker analysis in BRCA2-mutant patients: whether the olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed log-PFS contrast is larger in marker-D-positive than marker-D-negative disease. The expected raw interaction direction is uncertain, since marker D has a replicated prognostic association but has not modified osimertinib or sotorasib associations (H34–H35). A positive interaction of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Plausible alternatives are a marker-D prognostic effect without treatment selectivity, treatment allocation and disease-severity confounding, molecular co-segregation, small subgroup uncertainty, or chance.
chair_narrative: Register a distinct predictive-biomarker test among BRCA2-mutant patients: whether the olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed log-PFS contrast is greater in marker-D-positive than marker-D-negative disease. Marker D has a replicated clinically meaningful descriptive association with longer PFS (H19; R20–R21), but prior marker-D treatment interactions were near null (H24, H34, H35); thus the anticipated raw interaction is uncertain. A positive interaction of at least log(1.10)=0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Peer drafts differed on parent selection; I link to H3 because this refines the prior BRCA2–olaparib question, while explicitly citing marker-D evidence. Alternatives include a prognostic-only marker-D association, treatment allocation, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, baseline severity/inflammation, cohort structure, sparse subgroup uncertainty, and chance.

peer_narratives: H31 is negative: the independently validated stage-IV marker-D-by-CRP interaction is near zero (R46, 0.011; adjusted CI -0.028 to 0.050), with its upper bound below the clinically meaningful log(1.10)=0.095 threshold. H36 remains unresolved. Its validation estimate is modest (R45, 0.053) but the wide adjusted interval (-0.139 to 0.244) includes both no interaction and clinically meaningful olaparib-selective benefit; sparse BRCA2/marker/treatment cells preclude a clinically useful conclusion. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified adequately powered, covariate-adjusted BRCA2-mutant olaparib-by-marker-D interaction analysis, addressing treatment allocation and molecular/baseline prognostic confounding.

H36 remains unresolved after independent validation. The signed marker-D-by-olaparib interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease was 0.082 in discovery (R44) and 0.053 in validation (R45); the validation interval (-0.139 to 0.244 log-months) includes no interaction, harm, and a clinically meaningful benefit (>=log[1.10]≈0.095). Sparse four-cell subgroup data and unadjusted observational treatment allocation prevent a predictive conclusion. H31 is rejected: discovery and validation interactions for marker D by CRP status within stage IV disease were near null (R37, R46), and the validation upper bound (0.050) excludes the prespecified clinically meaningful positive interaction. The supported marker-D findings therefore remain descriptive prognostic associations rather than evidence of treatment selectivity. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified multivariable prognostic model for marker D incorporating disease burden, inflammatory markers, performance status, molecular features, and treatment allocation, while retaining treatment-by-marker terms as separate predictive estimands.
chair_narrative: H31 is rejected: both discovery and independent validation show a near-null stage-IV marker-D-by-CRP interaction (R37, R46), and the adjusted validation upper bound of 0.050 is below the clinically meaningful log(1.10)=0.095 threshold. H36 remains unresolved. Its discovery and validation estimates are positive but modest (0.082 and 0.053; R44, R45), while the validation interval (-0.139 to 0.244) includes no interaction, harm, and clinically meaningful olaparib-selective benefit. Sparse BRCA2-by-marker-by-treatment cells and unadjusted observational treatment allocation preclude a predictive conclusion. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified, adequately powered covariate-adjusted BRCA2-mutant olaparib-by-marker-D interaction analysis that addresses treatment allocation and baseline/molecular prognostic confounding.

peer_narratives: Run the two active prespecified BRCA2-mutant refinements. H37 estimates whether marker-D positivity has a prognostic association within BRCA2-mutant disease; H38 estimates the observational olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed contrast within the marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant subgroup. Use valid Welch independent-cell estimates and compare effects and 95% intervals with log(1.10)=0.095 as the clinical-significance benchmark. These analyses clarify whether the uncertain H36 interaction could reflect marker prognosis, a treatment contrast, or neither; neither can resolve confounding by treatment allocation or molecular/baseline covariation.

Analyze H37 and H38 to decompose the unresolved BRCA2-mutant marker-D/olaparib interaction. H37 estimates marker-D’s prognostic association within BRCA2-mutant disease; H38 estimates the unadjusted olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed contrast among marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant patients. Use valid Welch independent-cell estimates and 95% intervals, interpreting log-PFS effects against log(1.10)=0.095. These descriptive analyses cannot resolve observational treatment-allocation or molecular-confounding bias, but will distinguish a broadly prognostic marker association from the clinically relevant treated-subgroup contrast.
chair_narrative: Run the two active prespecified BRCA2-mutant refinements. H37 estimates the marker-D-positive versus negative prognostic contrast within BRCA2-mutant disease. H38 estimates the unadjusted olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed contrast among BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients. Use valid Welch independent-cell estimates and 95% intervals, interpreting log-PFS effects against log(1.10)=0.095 as the clinical-significance threshold. These analyses can distinguish marker prognosis from the treated-subgroup contrast, but neither resolves observational treatment-allocation, baseline, or molecular-confounding bias.

peer_narratives: H37’s unadjusted marker-D prognostic contrast in BRCA2-mutant disease is positive (0.125 log-months; R47), but its 95% interval (0.069 to 0.181) includes effects below the clinical-significance threshold of log(1.10)=0.095. It is compatible with the replicated overall marker-D association, but does not establish a clinically meaningful BRCA2-specific prognostic effect; molecular and baseline confounding remain plausible. H38 is below the clinical threshold at its point estimate (0.071) and its interval includes no effect as well as clinically meaningful benefit (R48). It is an unadjusted observational treatment contrast, so any apparent benefit could reflect treatment allocation and prognostic imbalance. Neither result supports a treatment-predictive conclusion or resolves H36.

H37 shows a positive marker-D association within BRCA2-mutant disease (0.125 log-months, 95% CI 0.069 to 0.181; R47). This is directionally consistent with the replicated overall marker-D association and supports a prognostic competing explanation for the putative olaparib-selective signal. The point estimate exceeds the clinical threshold of log(1.10)=0.095, but the interval includes effects below that threshold; it is an unadjusted, exploratory subgroup association and may reflect molecular or baseline confounding. H38 is unresolved: the unadjusted olaparib contrast in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients is 0.071 (95% CI -0.019 to 0.160; R48), spanning no benefit and clinically meaningful benefit. It cannot establish treatment benefit because of imprecision, multiplicity, and observational treatment-allocation confounding. Independent validation of H37 is useful to determine whether the prognostic alternative replicates.
chair_narrative: H37 shows a positive unadjusted marker-D prognostic association within BRCA2-mutant disease (0.125 log-months, 95% CI 0.069 to 0.181; R47), directionally consistent with the replicated overall marker-D association. However, its interval includes effects below the clinical-significance threshold of log(1.10)=0.095, and molecular or baseline confounding remains plausible. It supports a prognostic competing explanation but does not establish a clinically meaningful BRCA2-specific effect. H38 is unresolved: the unadjusted olaparib contrast among BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients is 0.071 (95% CI -0.019 to 0.160; R48), below the threshold at its point estimate and spanning no benefit and clinically meaningful benefit. This exploratory observational contrast is vulnerable to treatment-allocation and prognostic imbalance and cannot establish treatment benefit or resolve H36.

peer_narratives: H36 remains uncertain despite positive point estimates because its independent interval spans no interaction, harm, and a clinically meaningful predictive benefit (R44–R45). I propose decomposing that interaction. First, test whether marker-D positivity is prognostic within BRCA2-mutant disease; a positive association is expected from the replicated overall marker-D association (R20–R21), and would support the plausible alternative that any apparent interaction reflects prognosis rather than treatment selectivity. Second, estimate the olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed contrast specifically in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients. A positive contrast of at least log(1.10) would be clinically meaningful, but the raw direction is uncertain given the prior null BRCA2-specific olaparib interaction and observational treatment allocation. Alternative explanations include sparse-cell variation, baseline severity, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, and confounding by indication.

A focused follow-up is warranted for BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients: olaparib exposure versus non-exposure is hypothesized to increase log-PFS. H36’s positive but imprecise interaction estimates motivate this clinically interpretable within-biomarker contrast, although neither result establishes selective benefit. A log-PFS difference of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would meet the clinical-significance threshold. Plausible alternatives are no olaparib benefit, a prognostic rather than predictive marker-D association, treatment allocation bias, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, baseline severity/inflammation imbalance, sparse-cell uncertainty, and chance.
chair_narrative: H36 remains unresolved: its independent interval spans no interaction, harm, and clinically meaningful selective benefit. I therefore retain its uncertainty rather than treating its positive point estimates as predictive evidence. The first refinement tests whether marker-D positivity remains associated with longer PFS within BRCA2-mutant disease; a positive association is expected given the replicated overall marker-D association (R20–R21), and would support the plausible prognostic-only alternative. The second estimates the clinically interpretable olaparib exposed-minus-unexposed contrast in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients. Its raw direction is uncertain because H36 is imprecise and treatment allocation is observational; a positive effect of at least log(1.10)=0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Alternatives include no treatment benefit, confounding by indication, baseline severity/inflammation, BRCA2-linked molecular heterogeneity, sparse-cell variation, and chance.

peer_narratives: H37 is accepted as a positive unadjusted prognostic association: marker-D positivity in BRCA2-mutant disease was associated with longer log-PFS in discovery (0.125, R47) and independent validation (0.159, R49). The validation interval excludes zero, though includes effects below the clinical threshold of log(1.10)=0.095; thus clinical magnitude is not established with high precision. This association is not evidence that marker D predicts olaparib benefit, because baseline, molecular, and treatment-allocation confounding remain unresolved. H36 and H38 remain unresolved: available evidence cannot distinguish no clinically meaningful selective olaparib benefit from benefit or harm. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified covariate-adjusted olaparib-by-marker-D interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease, addressing treatment allocation and baseline prognostic imbalance.

H37 is accepted as a positive unadjusted prognostic association: independent validation estimates 0.159 log-months (R49), with its multiplicity-adjusted interval entirely above zero and directionally consistent with discovery. However, clinical magnitude remains uncertain because the lower bound (0.078) is below log(1.10)=0.095. This is not evidence of a BRCA2-specific or causal marker effect, given plausible molecular and baseline confounding. H36 and H38 remain unresolved regarding olaparib benefit or marker-D prediction: their sparse, unadjusted observational contrasts cannot distinguish treatment effect from allocation bias. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified covariate-adjusted olaparib-by-marker-D interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease, with adequate sparse-cell precision; validation of H38 alone would improve precision but not resolve confounding.
chair_narrative: H37 is accepted as a positive unadjusted prognostic association: marker-D positivity was associated with longer log-PFS within BRCA2-mutant disease in discovery (R47) and independent validation (R49). The validation interval excludes no association, but its lower bound (0.078) is below the clinical-significance threshold of log(1.10)=0.095, so clinically meaningful magnitude is not established precisely. This is not evidence of marker-D prediction of olaparib benefit or of a causal BRCA2-specific effect, because baseline and molecular prognostic confounding remain unresolved. H36 and H38 remain unresolved: sparse, unadjusted observational olaparib contrasts cannot distinguish clinically meaningful benefit, no benefit, or harm from treatment-allocation bias. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified covariate-adjusted olaparib-by-marker-D interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease, with adequate sparse-cell precision and adjustment for treatment allocation and baseline prognostic factors.

peer_narratives: Request the two remaining prespecified unadjusted olaparib contrasts within BRCA2-mutant disease: overall (H39) and marker-D-negative (H40). Together with the existing marker-D-positive estimate (H38) and interaction result (H36), these will quantify treatment contrasts in both marker strata. Use Welch independent-cell 95% intervals and interpret log-PFS effects against log(1.10)=0.095. Sparse strata and observational treatment allocation remain important limitations.

Run the two active, prespecified unadjusted olaparib contrasts in BRCA2-mutant disease: overall (H39) and marker-D-negative patients (H40). Together with H38, these estimate treatment contrasts in the full BRCA2 group and both marker strata, providing an interpretable check on the imprecise H36 interaction. Use valid Welch independent-cell 95% intervals and assess against log(1.10)=0.095 as the clinically meaningful benefit threshold. These estimates remain observational and susceptible to treatment-allocation, baseline prognostic, and molecular confounding; they cannot establish causal benefit without adjustment.
chair_narrative: Run the two active prespecified unadjusted olaparib contrasts in BRCA2-mutant disease: overall (H39) and marker-D-negative (H40). Together with marker-D-positive H38 and the imprecise interaction H36, these quantify treatment contrasts in both strata. Use Welch independent-cell 95% intervals and judge log-PFS effects against log(1.10)=0.095.
