peer_narratives: H39 provides no evidence of a clinically meaningful unadjusted olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant disease: the estimate is 0.028 log-months and its 95% interval (-0.032 to 0.089) remains below log(1.10)=0.095 at the upper bound. H40 similarly provides no evidence of clinically meaningful benefit in marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant disease (estimate -0.011; 95% CI -0.091 to 0.069), with the upper bound below the clinical threshold. Both are sparse, unadjusted observational treatment contrasts and remain susceptible to treatment-allocation and prognostic confounding; nevertheless, their intervals make further validation of these particular positive, clinically meaningful claims low priority.

H39 provides no support for clinically meaningful olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant disease: the unadjusted estimate is 0.028 log-months (95% CI -0.032 to 0.089; R50), with its upper bound below log(1.10)=0.095. H40 similarly rejects clinically meaningful benefit in the marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant stratum (estimate -0.011, 95% CI -0.091 to 0.069; R51). These results do not establish absence of a small effect and, as unadjusted observational contrasts, remain susceptible to treatment-allocation and prognostic confounding; however, neither justifies continued investigation of the proposed positive clinically significant effects. The sparse marker-D-positive contrast and interaction remain separately unresolved.
chair_narrative: H39 does not support a clinically meaningful positive unadjusted olaparib contrast in BRCA2-mutant disease: 0.028 log-months (95% CI -0.032 to 0.089; R50), with even the upper bound below log(1.10)=0.095. H40 likewise rejects clinically meaningful benefit in the marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant stratum (estimate -0.011, 95% CI -0.091 to 0.069; R51). These contrasts cannot establish absence of a small effect and are vulnerable to treatment-allocation, baseline prognostic, and molecular confounding, but neither warrants continued investigation of the proposed positive clinically significant effect. The sparse marker-D-positive contrast and treatment-by-marker interaction remain separately unresolved.

peer_narratives: I propose the directly interpretable olaparib contrast in all BRCA2-mutant patients, since H3 tested effect modification rather than the treated-versus-untreated contrast itself. A benefit of at least log(1.10)=0.095 would be clinically meaningful; plausible alternatives are no benefit, harm, or confounding by treatment allocation. I also propose the complementary marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant stratum, which—alongside active H38 in marker-D-positive patients—can show whether the uncertain H36 interaction reflects a reproducible difference in treated-group contrasts or sparse-cell variation. Given H36 and H38 uncertainty, the expected direction in this complementary stratum is deliberately uncertain. Both analyses remain observational and cannot eliminate baseline severity or molecular prognostic confounding.

Estimate the complementary unadjusted olaparib contrast among BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-negative patients. Together with H38, this makes the existing marker-D-by-olaparib interaction (H36) clinically interpretable by showing the treatment contrasts in both marker strata. The expected raw direction is uncertain: H36 has a positive but highly imprecise point estimate, while its validation interval spans meaningful benefit, no interaction, and harm. A contrast of at least log(1.10)=0.095 would meet the stated clinical-significance threshold. Any observed difference remains vulnerable to treatment-allocation bias, baseline prognostic imbalance, BRCA2 molecular heterogeneity, and sparse-cell uncertainty.
chair_narrative: I register the directly interpretable unadjusted olaparib contrast in all BRCA2-mutant patients and, to complement active H38, the corresponding contrast in marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant patients. The latter permits the uncertain H36 interaction to be interpreted as treatment contrasts in both marker strata rather than as an interaction estimate alone. Although one draft anticipated benefit in the overall BRCA2 group, I retain an uncertain raw direction because H3 rejected clinically meaningful effect modification and H36/H38 remain imprecise. A positive contrast of at least log(1.10)=0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Plausible alternatives are no benefit or harm, sparse-cell variation, and observational treatment-allocation, baseline severity, and molecular prognostic confounding.

peer_narratives: H36 remains unresolved. Independent validation estimates a small positive olaparib-by-marker-D interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease (0.053 log-months), but the interval is very wide (-0.139 to 0.244; R45) and includes clinically meaningful benefit, no interaction, and harm. Sparse cells and unadjusted observational treatment allocation preclude a predictive conclusion. H31 is rejected: validation shows no evidence that marker-D prognostic association differs by CRP stratum in stage-IV disease (0.011, interval -0.028 to 0.050; R46), and excludes a clinically meaningful positive interaction of log(1.10)=0.095. The most informative next action is independent validation of H38, the direct olaparib contrast in marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant disease, interpreted jointly with the already negative marker-D-negative contrast; this can sharpen the unresolved interaction while retaining caution about confounding.

H36 remains unresolved. Independent validation of the olaparib-by-marker-D interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease was positive but highly imprecise (0.053 log-months, interval -0.139 to 0.244; R45), encompassing no interaction, clinically meaningful benefit (log[1.10]≈0.095), and harm. Sparse cells and unadjusted observational treatment allocation preclude a predictive or causal conclusion. In contrast, H31 is rejected: its validation estimate was near null (0.011, interval -0.028 to 0.050; R46), and the upper bound is below the 10% clinical-significance threshold, excluding a clinically meaningful positive marker-D association difference by CRP status within stage IV disease. The supported finding remains prognostic association of marker D, not treatment-effect modification. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified covariate-adjusted olaparib-by-marker-D interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease, designed to improve sparse-stratum precision and address baseline prognosis and treatment-allocation confounding.
chair_narrative: H36 remains unresolved. Independent validation estimated a small positive olaparib-by-marker-D interaction within BRCA2-mutant disease (0.053 log-months; R45), but its wide interval (-0.139 to 0.244) includes no interaction, clinically meaningful benefit (log[1.10]≈0.095), and harm. Sparse cells and unadjusted observational treatment allocation preclude a predictive or causal conclusion. H31 is rejected: the validated CRP interaction estimate is near null (0.011, interval -0.028 to 0.050; R46), and its upper bound is below the clinical-significance threshold, excluding a clinically meaningful positive difference in the marker-D prognostic association by CRP stratum. The supported finding is marker-D’s prognostic association, not treatment-effect modification. The most informative next analysis is independent validation of H38, the direct olaparib contrast among marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant patients, interpreted alongside the negative marker-D-negative contrast (H40) and with continued caution regarding confounding.

peer_narratives: Analyze the three prespecified direct, unadjusted treatment contrasts in their biomarker-selected populations using Welch independent-cell 95% intervals. The clinical threshold is log(1.10)=0.095 log-months. Prior interaction estimates for osimertinib in EGFR-mutant disease (R1), sotorasib in KRAS-G12C disease (R2), and pembrolizumab by high PD-L1 (R4) were all near zero with intervals excluding or nearly excluding clinically important effect modification; these do not answer whether the treatments themselves have favorable contrasts within the selected populations. The requested analyses should report cell sizes and assess precision against 0.095. They remain observational, unadjusted contrasts and thus cannot establish causal treatment benefit because treatment allocation, baseline prognosis, and molecular covariates may confound estimates. The unresolved sparse olaparib marker-D-positive contrast (H38) remains better served by the available next validation request rather than repeated discovery analysis.

Analyze the three prespecified direct, unadjusted treatment contrasts in their biomarker-selected populations: osimertinib in EGFR-mutant disease (H41), sotorasib in KRAS-G12C disease (H42), and pembrolizumab in PD-L1 TPS≥0.5 disease (H43). Estimate exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS using Welch independent-cell intervals. Interpret a positive effect as clinically meaningful only if it is at least log(1.10)≈0.095 log-months; intervals wholly below this threshold will argue against a clinically meaningful benefit. These observational contrasts remain susceptible to treatment-allocation, prognosis, and molecular confounding, so even a precise association would not by itself establish causal treatment benefit.
chair_narrative: Run H41–H43: prespecified direct, unadjusted treatment contrasts within their biomarker-selected populations (osimertinib/EGFR-mutant, sotorasib/KRAS-G12C, and pembrolizumab/PD-L1 TPS≥0.5). Estimate exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS with Welch independent-cell 95% intervals, reporting cell sizes and precision against the clinical threshold log(1.10)=0.095. Earlier near-null interaction findings (R1, R2, R4) address effect modification rather than these within-selected-population contrasts. These observational associations remain vulnerable to treatment allocation, baseline prognosis, and molecular confounding and cannot alone establish causal benefit.

peer_narratives: All three unadjusted within-biomarker treatment contrasts are far below the clinical threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095. H41 (0.005, 95% CI -0.023 to 0.033; R52) and H42 (-0.001, -0.028 to 0.026; R53) exclude a clinically meaningful positive association. Although H43 is nominally positive (0.024, 0.004 to 0.044; R54), its entire interval remains below the clinical-significance threshold, so it does not support the registered clinically meaningful benefit claim. These observational contrasts also remain susceptible to treatment-allocation and prognostic confounding; validation would not make these small effects clinically important.

H41 and H42 reject clinically meaningful positive treatment contrasts: their 95% upper bounds (0.033 and 0.026 log-months; R52–R53) are well below log(1.10)≈0.095. H43 has a statistically positive but small unadjusted contrast (0.024, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.044; R54), also excluding the prespecified clinically significant threshold. All are observational, unadjusted associations susceptible to treatment-allocation, prognosis, and molecular confounding; this reinforces rather than weakens rejection of the proposed clinically meaningful benefits. Independent validation should prioritize the still-imprecise H38 marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant olaparib contrast, whose interval includes clinically important benefit.
chair_narrative: H41 and H42 reject clinically meaningful positive treatment contrasts: their 95% upper bounds (0.033 and 0.026 log-months; R52–R53) are well below log(1.10)≈0.095. H43 is statistically positive but small (0.024, 95% CI 0.004 to 0.044; R54), and its full interval likewise excludes the prespecified clinical-significance threshold. Thus none supports the registered clinically meaningful benefit claim. These are unadjusted observational contrasts and remain susceptible to treatment allocation, prognosis, and molecular confounding; this further precludes a causal efficacy conclusion. The participant drafts agree on rejection; the decision follows the clinical threshold rather than nominal significance.

peer_narratives: No new comparison is proposed. The priority remains independent validation of active H38, the direct olaparib contrast among BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients. Its discovery estimate (R48) is near the clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095 but is imprecise and includes no benefit. Adding further subgroup slices would worsen sparse-cell uncertainty rather than clarify whether marker D modifies olaparib benefit. Plausible alternatives remain no treatment benefit, chance variation, and unadjusted treatment-allocation or prognostic confounding.

I propose direct treatment contrasts in biologically selected populations. Rejected interaction claims H1, H2, and H4 indicate no clinically important evidence that these biomarkers modify treatment effects relative to their complements; they do not test whether the treated biomarker-defined population has a favorable treatment contrast itself. Expected benefit is positive log-PFS in EGFR-mutant osimertinib-treated patients, KRAS-G12C sotorasib-treated patients, and PD-L1-high pembrolizumab-treated patients. Effects of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would meet the stated clinical-significance threshold. Plausible alternatives are no meaningful benefit, harm, insufficient precision, or unadjusted treatment-allocation and prognostic confounding. H38 remains the most direct unresolved olaparib question and should be prioritized for independent validation rather than duplicated here.
chair_narrative: I register direct treatment contrasts in biologically selected populations. Rejection of H1, H2, and H4 excludes clinically meaningful biomarker effect modification, not a favorable treatment contrast within the biomarker-defined population itself. Each hypothesis expects positive log-PFS, with at least log(1.10)≈0.095 clinically meaningful. These are distinct from the sparse active olaparib question H38, which remains the priority for independent validation rather than duplication. Plausible alternatives for all new contrasts are no meaningful benefit, harm, inadequate precision, and unadjusted treatment-allocation, prognostic, or molecular confounding.

peer_narratives: H37 is supported as a positive marker-D prognostic association within BRCA2-mutant disease: discovery and independent validation are directionally concordant (R47, R49), with validation estimate 0.159 log-months. The validation lower bound (0.078) falls slightly below the prespecified clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095, so the existence of a positive association is supported but its reliably clinically significant magnitude remains uncertain. H38 is rejected: independent validation reverses the small discovery-positive estimate (-0.045 log-months, 99.6% interval -0.173 to 0.083; R55). Its upper bound is below 0.095, excluding a clinically meaningful positive olaparib contrast among marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant patients. Together with the negative marker-D-negative contrast, this provides no support for marker-D-guided olaparib benefit. These are unadjusted observational comparisons, so neither prognostic nor treatment conclusions establish causality. No validation capacity remains; the most informative subsequent analysis would be a confounding-adjusted treatment-effect analysis if the controller makes such an analysis available.

H37 remains supported as a prognostic association: independent validation shows higher log-PFS in marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant disease (0.159 log-months, R49), with a clearly positive interval. Its lower bound is below log(1.10)≈0.095, so the magnitude of a clinically significant association is not certain, but the directional association is robust and does not establish causality. H38 is rejected: validation of the direct olaparib contrast in marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant patients is negative (-0.045 log-months, R55), and its upper bound (0.083) is below the clinical-significance threshold. Together with the imprecise discovery result, this provides no support for clinically meaningful olaparib benefit in this subgroup. Sparse subgroup cells and unadjusted treatment allocation remain important limitations. The most informative next analysis would be an adjusted or otherwise confounding-robust estimate of olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant disease, rather than further marker-D subgroup splitting.
chair_narrative: H37 is supported as a positive prognostic association: both discovery and independent validation show higher log-PFS for marker-D-positive versus marker-D-negative BRCA2-mutant disease (R47, R49). Validation is positive (0.159 log-months), although its lower bound (0.078) falls below the prespecified clinically meaningful threshold, log(1.10)≈0.095; the presence of an association is supported, while certainty about a clinically meaningful magnitude is limited. H38 is rejected: validation reverses the small discovery-positive estimate (-0.045 log-months; R55), and its upper bound (0.083) is below the clinical-significance threshold. Thus there is no support for clinically meaningful olaparib benefit among marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant patients. This agrees with the negative marker-D-negative direct contrast, but all treatment comparisons are unadjusted observational associations and cannot establish causality. The most informative next analysis would be a confounding-robust adjusted estimate of olaparib effect in BRCA2-mutant disease rather than further marker-defined splitting.

peer_narratives: Run H44 and H45, the prespecified direct unadjusted pembrolizumab contrasts within TMB-high and STK11-mutant disease. For each, estimate exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS using Welch 95% intervals and compare the full interval with the clinical-significance threshold log(1.10)=0.095. These analyses address within-biomarker treatment-associated differences, whereas H5 and H6 addressed interaction effects. Interpretation will remain observational: treatment allocation and prognostic/molecular confounding can bias these unadjusted contrasts.

Analyze H44 and H45 as prespecified unadjusted mean log-PFS contrasts for pembrolizumab versus no pembrolizumab within TMB-high and STK11-mutant disease, respectively. Use Welch independent-cell 95% intervals and report cell sizes. Interpret a positive contrast of at least log(1.10)=0.095 as clinically meaningful; smaller statistically discernible associations will not support the registered clinically meaningful-benefit hypotheses. These observational comparisons remain susceptible to treatment-selection and prognostic confounding.
chair_narrative: Run H44 and H45, the prespecified unadjusted pembrolizumab contrasts within TMB-high and STK11-mutant disease. Estimate exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS using Welch independent-cell 95% intervals and report cell sizes. Judge clinical importance against log(1.10)=0.095: a nominally positive association whose interval remains below this threshold will not support clinically meaningful benefit. These direct within-subgroup contrasts answer a different question from the previously rejected interaction claims H5 and H6. peer_narratives: H44 and H45 provide no support for clinically meaningful pembrolizumab benefit within TMB-high or STK11-mutant disease. Their signed estimates are near null (−0.006 and 0.010 log-months), with 95% upper bounds of 0.011 and 0.034, respectively—well below log(1.10)≈0.095. Both analyses are unadjusted observational contrasts and would remain vulnerable to treatment-allocation and prognostic confounding even if a small association were present.

H44 and H45 do not support clinically meaningful positive pembrolizumab associations in TMB-high or STK11-mutant disease. The signed 95% intervals are respectively -0.024 to 0.011 (R56) and -0.013 to 0.034 log-months (R57), with upper bounds far below log(1.10)≈0.095. These precise null/subclinical unadjusted contrasts reject the registered benefit claims. Treatment allocation and prognostic or molecular confounding would also prevent interpreting these observational comparisons as causal efficacy estimates.
chair_narrative: H44 and H45 do not support clinically meaningful positive pembrolizumab associations within TMB-high or STK11-mutant disease. Their signed estimates are near null, with 95% upper bounds of 0.011 (R56) and 0.034 (R57) log-months, both well below log(1.10)≈0.095. These unadjusted observational contrasts also cannot support a causal efficacy interpretation because treatment allocation, prognosis, and molecular covariates may confound them.

peer_narratives: I propose direct, biomarker-selected pembrolizumab contrasts in TMB-high and STK11-mutant disease. Prior interaction results R5 and R6 address whether relative treatment associations differ by biomarker status, not whether pembrolizumab is associated with a clinically meaningful PFS advantage within either selected population. I expect a positive association in TMB-high disease and a possibly attenuated but still positive association in STK11-mutant disease; a log-PFS contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would meet the stated clinical threshold. Plausible alternatives are no meaningful benefit, harm, inadequate precision, or confounding from nonrandom treatment allocation and baseline prognosis. These unadjusted contrasts would not establish causal efficacy.

I propose reversals of H8 and H11 because their highly precise discovery estimates point to substantially higher, rather than lower, log-PFS in ECOG PS >=2 and NLR >=3 groups. The implied effects are far larger than log(1.10)≈0.095, but remain prognostic associations subject to confounding, selection, and possible construction artifacts. I also propose one-standard-deviation contrasts for each standardized research signature as an independent biomarker screen; direction is intentionally uncertain. Plausible alternatives are null or subclinical associations, reverse-direction associations, and noncausal correlations with prognosis or treatment allocation.
chair_narrative: I register direct, unadjusted pembrolizumab contrasts within TMB-high and STK11-mutant populations. H5 and H6 tested effect modification, not the clinically relevant treatment-associated log-PFS contrast within either selected population. A positive contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would be clinically meaningful; plausible alternatives are a subclinical or null association, harm, or confounding by treatment allocation, prognosis, and molecular features. I do not adopt the proposed reversals of H8/H11: those would be post-evidence reversals of already closed claims rather than prospectively motivated refinements. The proposed untargeted signature screen is also lower priority than resolving biologically interpretable treatment questions.

peer_narratives: No assessment deadlines or newly released validation require action. Supported findings include a reproducible, clinically meaningful positive prognostic association of research marker D with log-PFS overall and in several broad clinical subsets (notably H19, H22, H23, H29, H30, H32; independent validation intervals remain positive and generally exceed log(1.10)=0.095). H37 is also directionally replicated in BRCA2-mutant disease, but its validation lower bound is below 0.095, so clinically meaningful magnitude in that smaller subgroup remains uncertain. Negative findings are persuasive for clinically meaningful benefit from pembrolizumab within TMB-high or STK11-mutant disease (H44, H45; R56-R57 upper bounds well below 0.095), and for olaparib benefit in marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant disease (H38; R55). Treatment comparisons are unadjusted observational associations and do not establish causal treatment effects. The most informative next analysis is a confounding-robust multivariable treatment-effect analysis in BRCA2-mutant disease, with marker D evaluated as a prespecified effect modifier rather than further subgroup splitting.

H36 remains unresolved: independent validation is highly imprecise and includes clinically important benefit, no benefit, and harm. With no remaining validation capacity, further unadjusted marker-defined splitting is unlikely to resolve it. Supported findings remain marker-D’s reproducible positive prognostic association, including in BRCA2-mutant disease (H37), whereas direct targeted-treatment contrasts and tested treatment interactions provide no evidence of clinically meaningful benefit. The most informative next analysis is a confounding-robust adjusted olaparib comparison in BRCA2-mutant disease, rather than additional subgroup screens.
chair_narrative: Supported: marker-D positivity has a reproducible positive prognostic association with log-PFS overall and in multiple clinical subsets, including BRCA2-mutant disease (H19, H22, H23, H29, H30, H32, H37). For H37, validation is directionally positive (R49), supporting association presence, but its lower bound (0.078) is below log(1.10)=0.095, so clinically meaningful magnitude remains uncertain. Negative findings: unadjusted pembrolizumab contrasts in TMB-high and STK11-mutant disease do not support a clinically meaningful positive association (H44/H45; R56/R57 upper bounds below 0.095), and marker-D-positive BRCA2-mutant disease does not support clinically meaningful olaparib benefit (H38; R55 upper bound 0.083). H36 remains unresolved: R44/R45 are too imprecise to distinguish clinically important benefit, null effect, or harm; investigation is closed because validation capacity is exhausted. This resolves the drafts' emphasis differently: H37 supports a prognostic association but not assured clinical magnitude, whereas H36 cannot be converted to a negative conclusion. All treatment contrasts are unadjusted observational associations and do not establish causal efficacy. The most informative next analysis is a confounding-robust adjusted olaparib-effect analysis in BRCA2-mutant disease, with marker D prespecified as an effect modifier rather than further subgroup splitting.

peer_narratives: Run the three registered marker-D prognostic comparisons in KRAS-G12C disease (H46), ALK-fusion disease (H47), and stage-IV disease with brain metastases (H48). Use unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS Welch estimates with 95% intervals and inspect every cell size against the 20-observation requirement. Interpret clinical importance using log(1.10)=0.095: support for a clinically meaningful positive association requires a positive estimate with uncertainty compatible with or exceeding that threshold; intervals spanning null or materially sub-threshold effects will remain unresolved or be rejected as appropriate. These analyses test subgroup generalizability of the validated overall marker-D prognostic association, not causal effects, since molecular subtype, disease severity, treatment allocation, and other prognostic factors may confound unadjusted contrasts.

Analyze the three prespecified marker-D prognostic comparisons (H46–H48) using unadjusted exposed-minus-comparator mean log-PFS and Welch 95% intervals, requiring adequate cell sizes. These test molecular (KRAS-G12C, ALK fusion) and high-risk CNS-metastatic generalizability of the reproducible marker-D association. Clinical importance is assessed against log(1.10)=0.095: intervals wholly below this value would not establish a clinically meaningful association even if directionally positive. These are observational prognostic contrasts, so any association will not establish a causal marker effect.
chair_narrative: Run the three prespecified unadjusted marker-D prognostic comparisons in KRAS-G12C disease (H46), ALK-fusion disease (H47), and stage-IV disease with brain metastases (H48). Estimate marker-D-positive minus marker-D-negative mean log-PFS with Welch 95% intervals, verifying at least 20 observations per cell. Judge clinical importance against log(1.10)=0.095; positive associations with intervals materially below this threshold will not establish clinically meaningful magnitude. These test subgroup generalizability of H19, not causal marker effects, because unadjusted molecular, severity, and treatment differences may confound prognostic contrasts.

peer_narratives: All three marker-D subgroup contrasts are positive and their 95% lower bounds (0.131–0.142 log-months) exceed log(1.10)≈0.095, supporting clinically meaningful prognostic associations in these populations. The consistent magnitude also accords with the previously validated overall marker-D association. However, these are unadjusted observational subgroup comparisons amid substantial prior multiplicity; they do not establish causal or treatment-predictive effects, and molecular, disease-severity, and treatment-allocation confounding remain plausible. Validation capacity is exhausted, so these subgroup investigations are closed.

R58–R60 support positive, clinically meaningful prognostic associations of marker-D positivity in each prespecified subgroup: all estimates and 95% lower bounds exceed log(1.10)≈0.095. These subgroup results are consistent with the validated overall marker-D association, but are overlapping, not independent replications, and do not establish subgroup-specific heterogeneity. They are unadjusted observational contrasts and remain vulnerable to molecular, disease-severity, and treatment-allocation confounding; they should not be interpreted as causal marker effects or treatment-predictive findings. Validation capacity is exhausted, so further investigation is closed.
chair_narrative: R58–R60 support positive, clinically meaningful prognostic associations of marker-D positivity in each prespecified subgroup: every estimate and 95% lower bound exceeds log(1.10)≈0.095. These results are concordant with the independently validated overall marker-D association, but the subgroups overlap and are not independent replications or evidence of subgroup-specific heterogeneity. The sequential subgroup program creates multiplicity concerns, although the consistency and effect sizes make a null/clinically trivial association less plausible. All are unadjusted observational contrasts and remain susceptible to molecular, disease-severity, and treatment-allocation confounding; they do not establish a causal marker effect or treatment prediction. The peer drafts agree on this disposition; I retain it while explicitly limiting the interpretation to prognostic association. Validation capacity is exhausted, so investigations are closed.

peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has shown a reproducible positive prognostic association overall and across several clinical subsets, but its generalizability to molecularly defined KRAS-G12C and ALK-fusion populations remains untested. I propose prespecified within-genotype contrasts to test whether this association persists. A positive log-PFS contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would meet the stated clinical-significance threshold. Plausible alternatives are a subclinical or null association, a reversed association, or apparent heterogeneity arising from prognosis and treatment-allocation differences within genotype groups; these unadjusted contrasts would remain prognostic rather than causal.

I propose testing whether marker-D positivity retains its positive prognostic association in the clinically high-risk population with stage-IV disease and brain metastases. Marker D has shown a consistent positive association overall and across several subsets, but this CNS-metastatic setting has distinct prognosis and clinical relevance. A clinically meaningful positive contrast is approximately log(1.10)=0.095. Plausible alternatives are attenuation to a subclinical or null association in brain-metastatic disease, an adverse association, or an apparent association driven by residual prognosis or treatment-allocation confounding rather than marker biology.
chair_narrative: I combine the complementary drafts: test marker-D prognostic association in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, and clinically high-risk stage-IV brain-metastatic disease. H19 and its validated clinical-subset refinements support an anticipated positive association, but these populations have not been directly tested. A contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 is clinically meaningful. Plausible alternatives are attenuation below clinical importance, null or adverse associations, or apparent differences due to prognosis and treatment-allocation confounding; these are unadjusted prognostic comparisons, not causal marker effects. The drafts do not substantively conflict: molecular and CNS-metastatic generalizability address distinct gaps, so all are retained.

peer_narratives: Validation R55 does not support clinically meaningful olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive disease: the signed estimate is -0.045 log-months and its upper bound (0.083) is below log(1.10)≈0.095. Thus H38 is rejected. The interval still permits harm, so this is not evidence that olaparib is beneficial or harmless. More broadly, marker-D shows reproducible unadjusted positive prognostic associations, whereas available treatment-marker contrasts do not establish predictive or causal treatment benefit. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib treatment-effect model in BRCA2-mutant disease with marker D as an interaction term, rather than further unadjusted subgroup splitting.

H38 is rejected. Independent validation (R55) is incompatible with a clinically meaningful olaparib benefit among BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive patients: its signed 99.6%-level upper bound is 0.083, below log(1.10)≈0.095, and the point estimate is adverse. Together with the nonsignificant discovery result (R48), this does not support the proposed positive association. This is an unadjusted observational treatment contrast and is not causal efficacy evidence. The broader marker-D prognostic association remains supported, whereas treatment-effect modification and the imprecise H36 interaction remain unresolved. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib comparison in BRCA2-mutant disease, including marker D as an effect modifier rather than pursuing additional subgroup splits.
chair_narrative: H38 is rejected. Independent validation R55 estimates an adverse signed olaparib contrast (-0.045 log-months), and its upper bound (0.083) is below the clinically meaningful benefit threshold of log(1.10)=0.095. Thus clinically meaningful unadjusted olaparib benefit is not supported in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive disease; the interval still permits clinically important harm, so it does not establish safety or no effect. This agrees with the nonsignificant discovery result R48. Marker D retains a reproducible unadjusted positive prognostic association, but neither that association nor these treatment contrasts establishes causal efficacy or predictive treatment benefit. H36 remains unresolved because its interaction intervals remain too imprecise to distinguish benefit, null effect, and harm. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib comparison in BRCA2-mutant disease with marker D modeled as an effect modifier, rather than further unadjusted subgroup splitting.

peer_narratives: I request the three active, prespecified marker-D heterogeneity analyses (H49–H51). Each is an unadjusted Welch interaction: the marker-D-positive versus -negative log-PFS contrast in the specified subgroup minus that contrast in its complement. They directly test whether the reproducible overall prognostic association differs in KRAS-G12C disease, ALK-fusion disease, or stage-IV disease with brain metastases. Analyses should confirm all four interaction cells have n≥20 and report signed estimates with 95% Welch intervals. A clinically meaningful interaction requires approximately 0.095 log-months (log[1.10]); given prior near-null marker-D interactions, a precise interval below this magnitude would support consistency rather than subgroup specificity. These remain observational prognostic comparisons, not causal or treatment-predictive effects.

Run the three active, prespecified marker-D heterogeneity tests (H49–H51). Each estimates the signed difference in the marker-D-positive versus marker-D-negative log-PFS contrast between the named subgroup and its complement using Welch 95% intervals and requires at least 20 observations in each of four cells. The clinically meaningful differential threshold is log(1.10)≈0.095. These unadjusted interaction tests address heterogeneity of prognostic association, not causal marker effects or treatment prediction; prior broadly null interactions make a large positive differential uncertain.
chair_narrative: Request the three active prespecified marker-D heterogeneity analyses (H49–H51). Each is an unadjusted Welch interaction: the marker-D-positive versus -negative log-PFS contrast in the specified subgroup minus that contrast in its complement. Confirm all four interaction cells have n≥20 and report signed estimates with 95% intervals. A differential association of log(1.10)≈0.095 is clinically meaningful; precise intervals below this magnitude would support consistency rather than subgroup specificity. These are prognostic, observational comparisons, not causal or treatment-predictive effects.

peer_narratives: All three unadjusted marker-D interaction estimates are small and their 95% upper bounds (0.046, 0.063, and 0.031 log-months for R61–R63) are below the prespecified clinically meaningful heterogeneity threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095. Thus the data reject clinically meaningful positive amplification of the marker-D prognostic association in KRAS-G12C disease, ALK-fusion disease, or stage-IV disease with brain metastases. These are subgroup interaction tests within an observational dataset and do not address causal marker effects or treatment prediction; their consistency with prior null interactions supports a broadly similar unadjusted prognostic association rather than subgroup specificity.

R61–R63 provide no evidence that marker-D’s prognostic association is clinically meaningfully greater in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, or stage-IV brain-metastatic subgroups. All signed interaction estimates are small (0.007–0.021 log-months), their 95% intervals include no interaction, and—most importantly—the upper bounds (0.031–0.063) are below the prespecified clinically meaningful differential of log(1.10)≈0.095. These unadjusted subgroup contrasts therefore support consistency of the marker-D association rather than subgroup specificity. The overlap among subgroups and extensive prior subgroup testing further argue against interpreting minor numerical differences as biological effect modification. As observational Welch contrasts, they also cannot establish causal or predictive effects.
chair_narrative: R61–R63 do not support clinically meaningful positive amplification of the marker-D prognostic association in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, or stage-IV brain-metastatic disease. The signed interaction estimates are small (0.007–0.021 log-months), all intervals include no interaction, and their upper bounds (0.031–0.063) are below the prespecified clinically meaningful heterogeneity threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095. Thus these data support a broadly consistent unadjusted marker-D association rather than these specific forms of subgroup specificity. The subgroup tests are observational, unadjusted, overlapping, and part of an extensive subgroup-testing program; they cannot establish causal marker effects, biological effect modification, or treatment prediction.

peer_narratives: Marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful unadjusted positive prognostic association overall and in several molecular and high-risk clinical subgroups. The next useful question is heterogeneity, rather than further redundant within-subgroup main effects. I propose interaction tests for whether the marker-D contrast is larger in KRAS-G12C disease, ALK-fusion disease, or—within stage-IV disease—in patients with brain metastases. Effects are anticipated to be uncertain because prior marker-D interactions across stage, EGFR, histology, ECOG, CRP, and pembrolizumab exposure were near null. A positive interaction of at least log(1.10) would support clinically meaningful enrichment; plausible alternatives are a stable prognostic association across strata, attenuation in aggressive disease, or apparent heterogeneity from unadjusted molecular, severity, and treatment-allocation confounding. These are prognostic, not causal or treatment-predictive, comparisons.

Test whether the validated positive marker-D prognostic association generalizes to stage I–III disease and squamous histology. The overall association (R21) is clinically meaningful relative to log(1.10)≈0.095, while the prior stage and histology interaction results (R29, R32) do not support major attenuation in these complementary populations. I therefore anticipate positive direct contrasts, but leave both unresolved pending their direct estimates and intervals. Plausible alternatives are a clinically trivial or null association in either subgroup, or an apparent positive association driven by differing disease burden, molecular composition, or treatment allocation. These are unadjusted prognostic comparisons and cannot establish a causal marker effect.
chair_narrative: Marker-D positivity has clinically meaningful positive unadjusted prognostic contrasts overall and in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, and stage-IV brain-metastatic disease (H19, H46–H48). I therefore prioritize prespecified heterogeneity tests asking whether the contrast is greater in those populations; a positive interaction of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Anticipated direction is uncertain because prior marker-D interactions across stage, histology, ECOG, EGFR, CRP, and pembrolizumab were near null. Plausible alternatives are a stable association across strata, attenuation in aggressive disease, or apparent heterogeneity caused by molecular composition, severity, or treatment allocation. Peer 2's proposed direct contrasts in non-stage-IV and squamous disease are scientifically coherent but lower priority: existing precise stage and histology interaction results already make major attenuation in those complementary groups unlikely. These are unadjusted prognostic comparisons, not causal marker effects or treatment-predictive analyses.

peer_narratives:
Supported findings: marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful unadjusted favorable prognostic association (about 0.15–0.17 log-months, roughly 16–19% on the PFS-month scale) overall and across several examined strata, with independent support where available (R20–R21, R24–R25, R39–R41, R47–R49). High ECOG, high CRP, and stage IV status also show large unadjusted adverse associations where accepted; these are associations, not causal effects.

Negative findings: new subgroup interactions do not support clinically meaningful amplification of the marker-D association in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, or stage-IV brain-metastatic disease (R61–R63). Their upper confidence limits are all below the prespecified 10% relative-effect threshold (log[1.10]≈0.095). R55 reinforces rejection of H38: it provides no evidence of clinically meaningful unadjusted olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant, marker-D-positive disease and its upper bound is below 0.095.

Uncertainty remains for the marker-D-by-olaparib interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease (H36): available intervals remain compatible with meaningful benefit, null effect, or harm. All treatment and marker results are unadjusted observational contrasts and cannot establish treatment efficacy, safety, prediction, or biological effect modification. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib comparison among BRCA2-mutant patients, modeling marker D as an effect modifier rather than further unadjusted subgroup splitting.

No new validation or response deadline is present. Supported findings: marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful unadjusted positive association with log-PFS overall and across several examined populations (H19, H22, H23, H29, H30, H32, H37; validations R21, R25, R28, R35, R38, R41, R49). Its magnitude is roughly 0.15–0.17 log-months, exceeding log(1.10)≈0.095, but this is prognostic association rather than causal or treatment-predictive evidence. Negative findings: the marker-D associations do not show clinically meaningful amplification by stage, pembrolizumab, ECOG, histology, CRP, EGFR, KRAS-G12C, ALK fusion, or brain metastases where tested; notably R61–R63 have upper bounds below 0.095. Targeted-treatment benefit claims and treatment-interaction claims are generally unsupported, including olaparib benefit in BRCA2-mutant marker-D-positive disease (H38; R48, R55). Uncertainty remains for the olaparib-by-marker-D interaction in BRCA2-mutant disease (H36; R44–R45), whose broad intervals allow benefit, null effect, and harm. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib comparison among BRCA2-mutant patients, estimating marker-D effect modification without further unadjusted subgroup splitting.
chair_narrative: No new validation or response deadline is present. Supported findings are that marker-D positivity has a reproducible, clinically meaningful unadjusted favorable association with log-PFS overall and in several examined strata (H19, H22, H23, H29, H30, H32, H37; R20–R21, R24–R25, R28, R35, R38, R41, R49), approximately 0.15–0.17 log-months (about 16–19% on the PFS-month scale). High ECOG, high CRP, and stage-IV status also have large accepted unadjusted adverse associations where tested (H8, H10, H12–H15); these remain observational associations, not causal effects. Negative findings include no clinically meaningful positive amplification of the marker-D association in KRAS-G12C, ALK-fusion, or stage-IV brain-metastatic disease: R61–R63 have upper bounds below log(1.10)≈0.095. H38 remains appropriately rejected because validation R55 has an upper bound below that threshold for benefit, although it does not exclude clinically important harm. H36 remains unresolved: its interaction evidence (R44–R45) is compatible with meaningful benefit, no interaction, or harm. The peer drafts are substantively aligned; I retain the narrower conclusion of consistency only in the tested strata rather than claiming universal absence of heterogeneity. The most informative next analysis is a prespecified confounding-adjusted olaparib comparison among BRCA2-mutant patients, estimating marker-D effect modification directly rather than performing further unadjusted subgroup splits.

peer_narratives: Run H52, the prespecified unadjusted marker-D prognostic interaction by BRCA2 mutation status. Estimate the marker-D-positive versus -negative log-PFS contrast in BRCA2-mutant disease minus the corresponding contrast in non-mutant disease, verifying all four cells meet the n≥20 requirement and reporting the signed Welch 95% interval. A differential effect of log(1.10)≈0.095 or greater is clinically meaningful. This analysis addresses whether the favorable marker-D association seen within BRCA2-mutant disease (R47, R49) represents genuine heterogeneity rather than a broadly consistent prognostic association; it remains observational and cannot establish causality or treatment prediction.

Request analysis of H52: the unadjusted Welch interaction for the marker-D-positive versus -negative log-PFS contrast in BRCA2-mutant disease relative to its complement. Require all four cells to contain at least 20 observations and report the signed estimate with a 95% interval. I regard an interaction of log(1.10)≈0.095 or greater as clinically meaningful; a sufficiently precise interval below this threshold would support consistency of the prognostic association, whereas a wide interval spanning it would remain inconclusive. This observational interaction does not identify a causal biomarker effect or treatment prediction.
chair_narrative: Run H52, the prespecified unadjusted Welch interaction assessing whether the marker-D-positive versus -negative log-PFS contrast differs in BRCA2-mutant disease versus its complement. Verify all four cells have n≥20 and report the signed estimate and 95% interval. A differential contrast of log(1.10)≈0.095 or greater is clinically meaningful. This directly distinguishes the favorable association within BRCA2-mutant disease (R47, R49) from genuine prognostic heterogeneity; it remains observational and cannot establish causal biomarker effects or treatment prediction.

peer_narratives: R64 provides no support for positive amplification of the marker-D prognostic association in BRCA2-mutant disease. The signed interaction is negative and its upper 95% bound (0.029 log-months) is far below the prespecified clinically meaningful positive heterogeneity threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095. Although the lower bound permits modest attenuation, it does not reach that threshold either. This is an unadjusted, observational subgroup contrast from a broad, overlapping multiplicity-prone testing program, so it cannot establish biological interaction or causal biomarker effects.

R64 does not support clinically meaningful positive amplification of the marker-D prognostic association in BRCA2-mutant disease. The signed interaction is slightly negative (-0.027 log-months; 95% CI -0.084 to 0.029), and its upper bound is well below the prespecified clinically meaningful heterogeneity threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095. This rejects the positive interaction claim, while not establishing equality or excluding a clinically meaningful negative interaction because the lower interval bound remains near that threshold. As with prior marker-D subgroup analyses, this is an unadjusted, observational and multiplicity-prone comparison, so it cannot establish biology, causality, or treatment prediction.
chair_narrative: R64 rejects clinically meaningful positive amplification of the marker-D prognostic association in BRCA2-mutant disease: the signed interaction is -0.027 log-months (95% CI -0.084 to 0.029), with an upper bound well below the prespecified log(1.10)≈0.095 threshold. The interval also remains short of a clinically meaningful negative interaction. This supports consistency for this tested subgroup contrast, not biological interaction or causality, because the analysis is unadjusted, observational, and one of numerous overlapping subgroup tests.

peer_narratives: I propose a broader marker-D-by-high-CRP interaction, extending the stage-IV-specific null interaction in H31 to the full population. The hypothesis is that marker-D positivity has a larger favorable log-PFS association among patients with CRP >=10 mg/L; a clinically meaningful interaction is approximately 0.095 log-months or greater. This is falsifiable with the four marker-D/CRP cells. Prior R37 and R46 make substantial amplification within stage-IV disease unlikely, so the anticipated direction is uncertain. Plausible alternatives are a stable marker-D association regardless of inflammation, attenuation in inflammatory disease, or apparent heterogeneity due to disease severity, treatment allocation, or molecular composition. This remains an unadjusted prognostic comparison rather than evidence of a causal biomarker effect.

H36 remains unresolved because its validation interval is wide and compatible with meaningful marker-D modification of olaparib association, no modification, or harm. A clinically advanced stage-IV BRCA2-mutant refinement tests whether any such signal is concentrated in the population most relevant to systemic treatment. I anticipate no clear direction given the null overall BRCA2-mutant olaparib contrast (H39) and inconsistent marker-D-positive stratum result (H38). Plausible alternatives are no predictive interaction, apparent heterogeneity from treatment allocation or disease severity, or a true favorable association restricted to marker-D-positive advanced disease. This remains an unadjusted observational treatment comparison and cannot establish causal benefit.
chair_narrative: I prioritize a direct BRCA2-by-marker-D prognostic interaction. Marker-D positivity has a favorable association overall (R20–R21) and within BRCA2-mutant disease (R47, R49), but the available within-BRCA estimate does not establish whether the association is clinically meaningfully amplified or attenuated relative to non-BRCA2 disease. The hypothesis tests amplification; the anticipated raw direction is uncertain. A differential contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would be clinically meaningful. Plausible alternatives are a stable marker-D association across BRCA2 status, attenuation in BRCA2-mutant disease, or apparent heterogeneity from molecular composition, disease severity, or treatment allocation. This is an unadjusted prognostic comparison, not evidence of a causal biomarker effect. I do not adopt peer 1’s broader CRP interaction because the directly relevant stage-IV interaction, including validation, was near null (R37, R46), making broadening the population low yield. In BRCA2-mutant patients, the olaparib-by-marker-D interaction was 0.082 log-months in discovery (R44, 95% CI -0.038 to 0.201; cells 229–517) and 0.053 in independent validation (R45, stringent CI -0.139 to 0.244; cells 213–498), both using valid independent-cell Welch diagnostics. The validated estimate corresponds to only about 5% longer PFS, while its interval spans approximately 13% shorter to 28% longer PFS, including no interaction and effects exceeding the 10% clinical threshold (log[1.10]≈0.095). H36 therefore remains unresolved, not evidence for marker-guided olaparib use.

By contrast, marker-D positivity has a precise unadjusted prognostic association in the high-risk stage-IV/ECOG>=2 stratum (H56, R69: 0.136 log-months, 95% CI 0.111–0.160; n=2,484 versus 2,482; valid Welch diagnostic), equivalent to about 14.5% longer PFS and with the full interval above the clinical threshold. This is consistent with broader marker-D prognostic results, but is observational and cannot establish causality, mechanism, or treatment-effect modification. Tested marker-D interactions across clinical strata were generally near null or clinically subthreshold, and numerous treatment main-effect and interaction comparisons were null. The drafts substantively agree; the decision not to fragment H36 further follows from its limited BRCA2-mutant cell sizes, wide validated uncertainty, and lack of evidence supporting an additional post hoc modifier. A prespecified covariate-adjusted treatment-by-marker-D analysis within BRCA2-mutant patients would be more informative than further unadjusted splits.

Supported findings include a reproducible, clinically meaningful unadjusted favorable prognostic association of research-marker-D positivity with PFS overall (H19, R20-R21), with consistent associations in examined strata, including stage-IV/ECOG>=2 disease (H56, R69). Large adverse unadjusted prognostic associations for poor ECOG status, high CRP, and stage-IV disease are also supported (H8, H10, H12). These are observational prognostic findings, not causal effects or evidence for treatment selection.

Negative findings include near-null or clinically subthreshold tested treatment main effects and treatment-by-biomarker interactions for osimertinib, sotorasib, and pembrolizumab, as well as no convincing marker-D heterogeneity across tested clinical strata. The principal unresolved uncertainty is H36: the independently validated olaparib-by-marker-D interaction in BRCA2-mutant patients (R44-R45) remains compatible with clinically meaningful benefit, no interaction, and harm, and therefore cannot support marker-guided olaparib use.

The participant drafts agree on H18 and H36; this conclusion follows from the supplied validation intervals rather than vote counting. The most informative next analysis would be a prespecified covariate-adjusted olaparib-by-marker-D interaction analysis within BRCA2-mutant patients, addressing treatment allocation and major prognostic confounding rather than further small unadjusted subgroup splits.

peer_narratives: Run H57, the registered broad olaparib-by-marker-D interaction, as the remaining informative analysis. It tests whether the unresolved, sparse BRCA2-mutant interaction (H36; R44-R45) generalizes outside that restricted population. A signed interaction of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 would meet the clinical-significance threshold. Existing evidence suggests marker D is prognostic (for example H19, R20-R21) rather than predictive, since tested marker-D interactions have generally been near zero; nevertheless, H57 is needed to quantify this directly. A null or precise subthreshold estimate would argue against general marker-guided olaparib use, while a positive finding would remain observational and require careful consideration of treatment allocation and prognostic confounding.

Run H57, the prespecified broad olaparib-by-marker-D interaction. This tests whether any predictive association extends beyond the sparse BRCA2-mutant subgroup. A clinically significant interaction requires approximately 0.095 log-months (log[1.10]); prior marker-D findings are prognostic and prior treatment interactions have been near null, so this analysis should distinguish broad prediction from prognosis.
chair_narrative: Run H57, the prespecified broad olaparib-by-marker-D interaction. It directly tests whether the imprecise BRCA2-restricted signal in H36 generalizes to the full cohort. Prior marker-D results support a prognostic association, whereas tested marker-D treatment interactions have been near null; thus a precise subthreshold or null H57 result would favor prognosis rather than olaparib prediction. peer_narratives: H57 shows a precise near-null olaparib-by-marker-D interaction (R70: -0.005 log-months, 95% CI -0.025 to 0.014). The interval excludes a clinically meaningful positive interaction of approximately log(1.10)=0.095 and provides no support for marker-D-guided olaparib benefit. This broad null result also makes the sparse BRCA2-restricted H36 signal more plausibly sampling variability; marker-D’s repeated unadjusted associations are better viewed as prognostic and potentially confounded rather than predictive.

chair_narrative: Register a broader olaparib-by-marker-D interaction to test whether any predictive association generalizes beyond the sparse BRCA2-mutant cells. Run H58, the prespecified marker-D prognostic association among patients unexposed to all four recorded agents. The analysis is an unadjusted Welch mean difference in log-PFS for marker-D-positive versus -negative patients, requiring at least 20 observations per cell. A favorable contrast of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 log-months is considered clinically meaningful. chair_narrative: Run H58: an unadjusted Welch mean difference in log-PFS comparing marker-D-positive with marker-D-negative patients unexposed to all four recorded therapies, requiring at least 20 patients per cell. This is a clinically interpretable robustness test of the established favorable marker-D association (H19, R20–R21) outside recorded agent exposure. A favorable difference of at least log(1.10)≈0.095 log-months is clinically meaningful. peer_narratives: H58 shows a favorable unadjusted marker-D association in patients unexposed to all four recorded therapies (R71: 0.153 log-months, 95% CI 0.130 to 0.175). The entire interval exceeds the prespecified clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095, and its consistency with the overall marker-D finding supports acceptance of this descriptive association. However, restriction to the untreated stratum can induce selection bias, and the unadjusted contrast remains vulnerable to baseline prognostic confounding; it does not establish that marker D causally improves PFS or has treatment-selection utility. Given no remaining validation requests and the result’s role as a robustness association rather than a causal test, investigation is closed.

H58 shows a precise favorable unadjusted association for marker-D positivity among patients unexposed to all four recorded agents (R71: 0.153 log-months, 95% CI 0.130 to 0.175). The entire interval exceeds the clinically meaningful threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095, supporting a clinically significant prognostic association in this stratum. This does not establish a causal marker effect or treatment-independent biology: conditioning on absence of recorded therapies can induce selection bias, and residual disease-severity, eligibility, and unmeasured-treatment confounding remain plausible. Nevertheless, persistence outside recorded-agent exposure argues against the overall association being solely a simple consequence of exposure to those agents.
chair_narrative: H58 supports a clinically meaningful unadjusted association: among patients unexposed to all four recorded therapies, marker-D positivity was associated with higher log-PFS by 0.153 log-months (R71, 95% CI 0.130 to 0.175), with the full interval exceeding log(1.10)≈0.095. This is consistent with the previously replicated overall marker-D association, although this post hoc robustness stratum should not be treated as independent confirmation after the broader exploratory program. Conditioning on receiving no recorded therapy can induce selection/collider bias, and baseline prognosis, treatment eligibility, and unrecorded care remain plausible confounders. Thus acceptance is limited to the descriptive prognostic association in this selected stratum; it neither establishes causality nor supports treatment-selection utility.

peer_narratives: Test whether marker-D positivity retains its favorable prognostic association among patients receiving none of the four recorded systemic agents. Persistence would support a broadly prognostic rather than drug-specific marker-D association; attenuation could indicate treatment allocation, therapy-associated selection, or confounding by unmeasured disease features. peer_narratives: H59 is supported as a descriptive reversed-direction association. ECOG PS >=2 had higher log-PFS by 0.447 (95% CI 0.435–0.459) in discovery and 0.449 (stringent validation CI 0.431–0.467) in validation (R8, R13). This is far above the clinical threshold of log(1.10)=0.095, corresponding to roughly 57% longer PFS on the raw ratio scale. Welch cell sizes were ample and diagnostics were valid. The result is internally precise but clinically counterintuitive and observational; it does not establish that worse performance status improves PFS, given likely coding, selection, treatment-allocation, or residual-confounding explanations. It reverses the originally negative-direction H8 claim, which remains rejected.

H59 is accepted as a descriptive positive-direction association. The signed discovery and stringent validation estimates are 0.447 (95% CI 0.435 to 0.459; R8) and 0.449 log-months (0.431 to 0.467; R13), respectively. Both greatly exceed the clinical threshold of log(1.10)≈0.095, corresponding to an approximately 57% higher geometric mean PFS. The large, consistent effect is opposite to H8's originally negative-direction claim, which remains correctly rejected. This unadjusted observational contrast is not causal: nonstandard coding, treatment selection, survival/selection processes, and uncontrolled prognostic confounding could plausibly explain it.
chair_narrative: H59 is accepted as a descriptive positive-direction association. Welch comparisons were valid with large cells. Both intervals are well above the clinical threshold log(1.10)=0.095. This reverses H8's adverse-direction claim, which remains rejected because its signed estimates oppose that claim. The result is an unadjusted observational association, not evidence that poorer performance status improves PFS; coding, treatment allocation, selection, and residual prognostic confounding remain plausible explanations. No null finding is suggested for the descriptive positive association.

Its magnitude (~0.45 log-months) greatly exceeds log(1.10)≈0.095. This counterclinical result is falsifiable by re-estimating the positive-direction contrast. Plausible alternatives include reversed or nonstandard coding, treatment-selection or survivorship bias, and severe unmeasured confounding; even if confirmed descriptively, it would not support a causal benefit of poor performance status.
